The frog opened his lips and said, "I am looking for a place to rest, just like you. Would you like to stay here with me?"

The duck thought about it and decided that it sounded nice. He agreed and they became friends. They would spend their days wandering together through the tall yellow flowers, playing and exploring.

The duck and frog were happy, until one night a deep thunderstorm came and brought a flood that sent them both away. But even though they had to wander apart, their friendship still remained. Every day, when the sun shone and the flowers bloomed, the duck wondered if his friend was still there, hopping and chatting in the open field.

Lily learned that sometimes trying something different doesn't always work out. She decided to stick with the candies she knew she liked and saved her pennies for something else.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys on the rug in the living room. The rug was soft and hairy and had many colors. They liked to make noises and pretend they were animals or cars or superheroes.

But their mom was trying to work on her laptop at the table. She had a lot of papers and books and pens. She needed to be quiet and think hard. She did not like the noises that Tom and Lily made. They disturbed her.

"Tom, Lily, please be quiet. You are disturbing me. I have to work. Can you play somewhere else?" she asked.

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They did not want to leave the rug. They liked the rug. It was their favorite place to play.

"But mom, we like the rug. It is soft and hairy and has many colors. We are having fun. Can we stay here?" they said.

Mom sighed. She loved Tom and Lily, but she also had to work. She had an idea.

"How about this? You can stay on the rug, but you have to play quietly. No noises, no shouting, no jumping. Just whisper and move slowly. Can you do that?" she said.

Tom and Lily nodded. They wanted to make mom happy. They decided to play quietly. They whispered and moved slowly. They pretended they were mice or snails or fairies.

Mom smiled. She was glad that Tom and Lily were quiet. They did not disturb her. She could work. She thanked them.

"Tom, Lily, thank you for being quiet. You are very good. I appreciate it. When I finish my work, we can have a snack and read a story. How does that sound?" she said.

Tom and Lily smiled. They were happy. They liked snacks and stories. They hugged mom.

"That sounds great, mom. We love you. You are the best." they said.

Tom is a young kid who likes to play with his cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He likes to make them zoom and crash on the floor. He thinks his cars are the best toys ever.

One day, he goes to the park with his mom. He sees another kid playing with a big truck. The truck has lights and sounds and can move by itself. Tom thinks the truck is very cool. He wants to play with it too.

He runs to the other kid and says, "Can I play with your truck? It is so cool!" The other kid looks at Tom and says, "No, this is my truck. You can't play with it. Go away!"

Tom feels sad and angry. He says, "That is not nice. You should share your toys. I have many cars. I can share them with you." The other kid says, "I don't want your cars. They are boring. My truck is better. Leave me alone!"

Tom starts to cry. He runs back to his mom. He hugs her and says, "Mom, that kid is mean. He won't let me play with his truck. He says my cars are boring. I don't like him."

His mom hugs him back and says, "I'm sorry, Tom. Some kids are not very friendly. But you are a good kid. You are kind and generous. You know how to share your toys. I'm proud of you."

Tom feels a little better. He realizes that his mom is right. He is a good kid. He doesn't need the truck. He still likes his cars. He says, "Thank you, mom. I love you. Can we go home and play with my cars?"

His mom smiles and says, "Of course, Tom. I love you too. Let's go home and play with your cars." They hold hands and walk home. Tom forgets about the truck and the mean kid. He is happy with his mom and his cars.

Tom and Lily were playing with bricks in the garden. They liked to build towers and houses and castles with the bricks. They had many bricks of different colors and shapes.

"Look at my tower, Lily!" Tom said. "It is very tall and strong. I am the king of the tower."

Lily looked at Tom's tower. She did not like it. She thought it was too big and boring. She wanted to make her own tower. She took some bricks from Tom's tower and put them on her pile.

"Hey, stop that!" Tom said. "Those are my bricks. You cannot take them. Give them back!"

Lily did not listen. She was bossy. She said, "No, I need them for my tower. My tower is better than yours. I am the queen of the tower."

Tom was angry. He tried to grab the bricks from Lily, but she pushed him away. They started to fight over the bricks. They pulled and pushed and shouted.

Suddenly, a big dog appeared in the garden. It was brown and furry and had a loud bark. It saw the bricks and thought they were toys. It ran towards Tom and Lily and jumped on their towers. It knocked down the bricks and made a big mess.

Tom and Lily were scared. They stopped fighting and ran away from the dog. They hid behind a bush and watched the dog play with the bricks.

"Look what the dog did!" Tom said. "It ruined our towers. Now we have no bricks to play with."

Lily felt sorry. She said, "I am sorry, Tom. I should not have been bossy. I should have shared the bricks with you. Can we be friends again?"

Tom nodded. He said, "I am sorry, too. I should not have been mean. I should have let you make your own tower. Yes, we can be friends again."

They hugged and smiled. They decided to wait until the dog left and then build a new tower together. They learned to be nice and share. They had fun with the bricks.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big pond with many ducks. They also see a small yacht on the water. It is a toy yacht. It has a sail and a flag.

"Wow, look at the yacht!" Tim says. "It is so cool. Can we play with it?"

"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe it belongs to someone."

They go closer to the pond. They see a man sitting on a bench. He has a remote control in his hand. He is making the yacht move on the water.

"Excuse me, sir," Tim says. "Can we play with your yacht, please?"

The man looks at Tim and smiles. "Sure, you can," he says. "But be careful. Don't make it crash or sink."

"Thank you, sir," Tim says. He takes the remote control from the man. He gives it to Mia. "You go first," he says.

Mia holds the remote control. She presses a button. The yacht moves forward. She presses another button. The yacht turns left. She presses another button. The yacht turns right. She is having fun.

Tim watches Mia. He is happy for her. He also wants to play with the yacht. He waits for his turn.

Meanwhile, the ducks see the yacht. They are curious. They swim towards it. They think it is food. They peck at it. They try to pull it. They make loud noises.

"Hey, stop that!" Mia says. "That is not food. That is a toy. Go away, ducks!"

But the ducks do not listen. They keep pecking and pulling. The yacht is in trouble. It is tipping and spinning. It is getting wet.

"Oh no!" Tim says. "The yacht is going to sink. Give me the remote control. I will save it."

Mia gives the remote control to Tim. Tim presses the buttons. He tries to make the yacht move away from the ducks. But it is too late. The ducks are too strong. They flip the yacht over. It sinks under the water.

"Uh oh," Tim says. "We broke the yacht. We are in trouble."

The man sees what happened. He runs to the pond. He is angry. He is sad. He is embarrassed.

"What did you do?" he says. "You ruined my yacht. It was a gift from my son. It was very expensive. How could you be so careless?"

Tim and Mia are scared. They are sorry. They are embarrassed. They do not know what to say.

Their moms hear the man. They come to the pond. They see the yacht under the water. They see the ducks swimming away. They see the man yelling. They see Tim and Mia crying.

They are shocked. They are confused. They are embarrassed. They try to calm the man. They try to comfort Tim and Mia. They try to explain what happened.

They are in a big mess. They wish they never saw the yacht. They wish they never played with it. They wish they never fed the ducks.

Lila was a little girl who liked to play in the woods. She had a friend who lived in the woods. His name was Zee. Zee was a spirit. He was not like other people. He was smooth and shiny and could fly and change shape.

One day, Lila and Zee were playing hide and seek. Lila counted to ten and then looked for Zee. She looked behind the trees, under the rocks, and in the flowers. But she could not find Zee. She called his name, but he did not answer.

Lila felt sad and scared. She thought Zee had left her. She sat on a log and cried. Then she heard a soft voice in her ear. It was Zee. He said, "Don't cry, Lila. I'm here. I was hiding in the sun. You could not see me because I was too bright. I'm sorry I made you sad. I love you, Lila. You are my best friend."

Lila smiled and hugged Zee. She said, "I love you too, Zee. You are my best friend. You are a very good hider. But next time, please don't hide in the sun. I want to see you and play with you."

Zee nodded and said, "OK, Lila. Next time, I will hide somewhere else. Somewhere you can find me. But you have to be very smart and very fast. Because I am a spirit, and I can do many things."

Lila and Zee laughed and played some more. They had fun in the woods. They were happy. They were friends.

Lily and Max are at the beach with Mom and Dad. They play in the sand and make a big castle. They find some shells and stones and put them on the castle. They are very happy.

"Look, Mom, look, Dad, our castle is so pretty!" Lily says.

"Yes, it is, you did a great job!" Mom says.

"Can we go in the water, please?" Max asks.

"OK, but be careful, the waves are big today," Dad says.

Lily and Max run to the water and splash each other. They laugh and scream. The waves are fun, but they are also strong. They push Lily and Max back to the shore.

"Wow, that was fun, but I'm tired now," Lily says.

"Me too, let's go back to our towels and nap," Max says.

They walk back to their towels and lie down. Mom and Dad join them and cover them with a blanket. The sun is warm and the wind is soft. Lily and Max close their eyes and nap.

They dream of the beach and the waves and the castle. They dream of the brown dog that ran by and barked at them. They dream of the ice cream they will have later. They are very happy.

Tom and Sue were twins who liked to play together. They had a big box of toys in their room, but they wanted to share some with their cousin Amy, who lived far away. They decided to mail some toys to Amy as a surprise.

They picked out some toys that they thought Amy would like: a ball, a doll, a car, and a book. They put them in a big envelope and wrote Amy's name and address on it. Then they asked their mom to take them to the post office.

At the post office, they gave the envelope to the man behind the counter. He put a stamp on it and said, "This will take a few days to get to Amy. She will be very happy when she opens it."

Tom and Sue were impatient. They wanted Amy to get the toys right away. They asked their mom, "Can we call Amy and tell her we mailed her something?"

Their mom said, "No, that would spoil the surprise. You have to wait until she gets it and calls you back. That will be more fun."

Tom and Sue were not happy. They wanted to talk to Amy now. They pouted and whined all the way home.

When they got home, they saw a package on the porch. It had their names on it. They ran to open it. Inside, they found a letter and a jar of jelly. The letter said, "Dear Tom and Sue, thank you for being such good cousins. I miss you a lot. I made this jelly for you with grandma. I hope you like it. Love, Amy."

Tom and Sue were very surprised and happy. They hugged the jar of jelly and ran to show their mom. They said, "Look, mom, Amy mailed us something too! She made us jelly! Can we eat some now?"

Their mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. That was very nice of Amy. Why don't you call her and say thank you?"

Tom and Sue agreed. They called Amy and thanked her for the jelly. They told her they mailed her some toys. They chatted and laughed for a while. They felt closer to Amy, even though she lived far away. They learned that mailing and receiving things can be fun, but also that they have to be patient sometimes.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They saw a big box of muffins on the table. They wanted to eat them, but Mom said no. She said they were for Grandma, who was coming to visit.

Tim and Kim waited until Mom went to the bathroom. Then they ran to the table and grabbed two muffins each. They stuffed them in their mouths and smiled. They were very yummy.

But then they heard Mom coming back. They were scared. They did not want Mom to see them. They looked for a place to hide. They saw the oven. It was big and dark. They opened the door and crawled inside.

"Where are the muffins?" Mom asked, when she saw the empty box. She looked around and saw the oven door open. She was angry. She thought someone had left it open by mistake. She did not know Tim and Kim were inside. She shut the door and turned on the oven.

Tim and Kim felt the heat. They felt the pain. They screamed and cried. They banged on the door. But Mom did not hear them. She was busy setting the table for Grandma. She was glad to see her.

The end.

Tom and Lily liked to help Mom with the dishes. They put the dirty plates and cups in the dishwasher. Then they pushed the buttons to make it start. They heard the water and the soap inside.

"Look, it is washing the dishes for us!" Tom said.

"Yes, it is very clever!" Lily said.

They watched the dishwasher for a while. Then they got bored. They decided to play a game. They took turns to make funny faces and noises. They tried to make each other laugh.

Tom stuck out his tongue and crossed his eyes. Lily giggled. Lily wrinkled her nose and snorted like a pig. Tom laughed. They made more faces and noises. They laughed louder and louder.

Mom heard them from the living room. She smiled. She was happy that they were having fun. She was also happy that they helped her with the dishes. She thought they were very successful helpers. She went to join them and play with them. They all laughed together.

Lily was happy to introduce her new friend, Max, to her mom and dad. Max was a big dog with brown fur and a long tail. He followed Lily everywhere and played with her toys. Lily found Max in the park when she was with her nanny. He had no collar or tag, so Lily decided to take him home.

"Can I keep him, please?" Lily asked her mom and dad. "He is so nice and cute and he likes me a lot."

Her mom and dad looked at each other and frowned. They knew that Max was an expensive dog, and that someone must be looking for him. They also knew that they did not have enough money or space for a big dog like Max. But they did not want to make Lily sad, so they said, "OK, you can keep him for one night, but tomorrow we have to find his real owners."

Lily was so happy that she hugged Max and thanked her mom and dad. She gave Max some food and water, and then took him to her room. She made a bed for him with her blankets and pillows, and told him stories until they both fell asleep.

The next morning, Lily woke up to a loud noise. She opened her eyes and saw that Max had chewed up her books, her dolls, her clothes, and her shoes. He had also made a big mess on the floor and the walls. Lily started to cry, and her mom and dad came running to see what was wrong.

They were shocked and angry when they saw the damage that Max had done. They scolded Lily and Max, and told them that they had to get rid of Max right away. They called the animal shelter, and a man came to take Max away. Lily begged them to let her keep Max, but they said no. They said that Max was a bad dog, and that they could not afford to fix the things he had ruined. They said that Lily had to learn to be more careful and responsible.

Lily watched as Max was put in a cage and taken away. She felt very sad and sorry. She wished she had never introduced Max to her mom and dad. She wished she had never found him in the park. She wished she had a different friend, one that was not so expensive and naughty. She wondered if Max would ever find his real owners, or if he would stay in the shelter forever. She hoped he would be happy, but she doubted it. She knew she would never see him again.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play at the park. The park has a lot of equipment. There is a slide, a swing, a seesaw and a climbing frame.

One day, Anna and Ben go to the park with their moms. They run to the equipment and have fun. Anna likes the slide. She goes up and down, up and down. Ben likes the swing. He pushes himself high, high, high.

"Look at me, Anna!" Ben says. "I can swing so high!"

"Wow, Ben, you are so brave!" Anna says. "Can you see the birds?"

"Yes, I can see them. They are flying in the sky. Do you want to try the swing?"

"OK, Ben, I will try. But first, let me show you something. Come with me to the climbing frame."

Anna and Ben go to the climbing frame. It is big and has many bars and ropes. Anna likes to climb. She can climb to the top and see the whole park.

"Look at me, Ben!" Anna says. "I can climb so high!"

"Wow, Anna, you are so strong!" Ben says. "Can you see the flowers?"

"Yes, I can see them. They are colorful and pretty. Do you want to try the climb?"

"OK, Anna, I will try. But first, let me tell you something. I have a surprise for you. Come with me to the bench."

"Yes, I am hungry. Let's eat!"

They thank their moms for the yummy snack. Then they go back to the equipment and play some more. They slide, they swing, they seesaw and they climb. They have a lot of fun. They are friends.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to study the sea. They had a big book with pictures of fish, crabs, shells and seaweed. They wanted to learn the names of all the things that lived in the water.

One day, they went to the shore with their book and a bucket. They saw the waves splash and the sand sparkle. They looked for things to put in their bucket. They found a starfish, a snail, a clam and a feather.

"Look, Mia, I found a starfish!" Tom said. "It has five arms and it is red and bumpy."

"Wow, Tom, that is a nice starfish!" Mia said. "I found a snail. It has a shell and it is slimy and slow."

They put their things in the bucket and looked at their book. They matched the pictures with the things they found. They learned the names of the starfish, the snail, the clam and the feather.

Then they saw something shiny in the water. It was a big fish with scales and a fin. It was swimming near the shore.

"Look, Mia, a fish!" Tom said. "It is shiny and fast. Do you think it is friendly?"

"I don't know, Tom," Mia said. "It is big and it has teeth. Maybe it is hungry."

They were curious about the fish, but they were also scared. They wanted to study the fish, but they did not want to get hurt.

They decided to be brave and go closer to the water. They held hands and walked slowly. They kept their bucket and their book with them.

They reached the edge of the water and looked at the fish. The fish looked at them and made a noise.

"Hello, fish!" Tom said. "We are Tom and Mia. We are studying the sea. What is your name?"

The fish did not answer. It swam away and disappeared.

Tom and Mia were disappointed, but they were also proud. They had been brave and they had seen a new thing. They went back to their bucket and their book. They had more things to study and more stories to tell.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play outside with their ball. But today it is very hot and sunny. Sam and Ben feel uncomfortable. They are thirsty and sweaty.

"Can we go inside, Sam?" Ben asks. "I want some water and a snack."

Sam nods. He is also tired of the heat. He picks up the ball and walks to the house. But when they get to the door, they see their mom.

"Hi, boys," mom says. "Did you have fun outside?"

"Yes, mom," Sam and Ben say.

"Good. But before you go inside, I have something to remind you. You need to do your exercise. Remember what the doctor said? You have to move your bodies every day to be healthy and strong."

Sam and Ben groan. They don't want to do exercise. They want to rest and cool down.

"Please, mom," Ben says. "Can we do it later? It's too hot now."

Mom shakes her head. She smiles. "No, boys. You have to do it now. It won't take long. And I have a surprise for you. If you do your exercise, you can have some ice cream afterwards. How does that sound?"

Sam and Ben perk up. They love ice cream. They look at each other. Maybe exercise is not so bad after all.

"Okay, mom," Sam says. "What do we have to do?"

Mom shows them some simple exercises. They have to jump, run, stretch, and bend. Sam and Ben follow mom. They feel their hearts beat faster and their muscles work. They also feel more happy and energetic.

"Good job, boys," mom says. "You did your exercise. I'm proud of you. Now you can go inside and have some ice cream. You earned it."

Sam and Ben cheer. They thank mom and run inside. They enjoy their ice cream. They feel good. They are glad they did their exercise. They decide to do it again tomorrow.

Lila and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big red truck with a sign that says "Oxygen". They are curious and want to look inside.

"Let's go see what's in there!" Ben says.

"No, Ben, that's dangerous!" Lila says. "Oxygen is something we breathe, but too much can make fire or hurt us. Mama told me that."

"But I want to see!" Ben says. He runs to the truck and opens the door.

Lila follows him and sees many big metal bottles with tubes and masks. She hears a hissing sound and smells something strange.

"Ben, stop! This is not a toy!" Lila says. "We have to get out of here!"

But Ben does not listen. He grabs a mask and puts it on his face. He starts to feel dizzy and sick.

"Ben, what are you doing?" Lila says. She tries to pull the mask off him, but he pushes her away.

Suddenly, they hear a loud voice.

"Hey, you kids! Get away from that truck! That's not for you! That's for sick people who need oxygen!" The voice belongs to a man in a white coat. He is a doctor who works at the hospital. He was delivering the oxygen to the patients.

He runs to the truck and sees Ben and Lila. He is angry and scared.

"What are you doing here? Do you know how dangerous this is? You could have started a fire or hurt yourself!" He says. He takes the mask off Ben and checks his pulse. He is relieved that Ben is still breathing.

He turns to Lila and says, "You, young lady, you should have known better. Why did you let him do that?"

Lila feels ashamed and sorry. She says, "I'm sorry, sir. I tried to stop him, but he didn't listen. I told him it was dangerous, but he was curious. I didn't mean to cause trouble."

The doctor sighs and says, "Well, I'm glad you're both okay. But you should never play with oxygen or anything you don't know. It could be very bad for you. Next time, if you see something like this, stay away and tell an adult. Do you understand?"

Lila and Ben nod and say, "Yes, sir. We understand."

The doctor says, "Good. Now, go back to your parents and don't do this again. And I recommend you to drink some water and rest. You might feel a little sick from the oxygen."

Lila and Ben say, "Thank you, sir. We're sorry, sir." They run back to their parents and tell them what happened. Their parents are shocked and angry, but also relieved that they are safe. They hug them and scold them and make them promise to be more careful. Lila and Ben learn their lesson and never play with oxygen again.

"Look, Lily, there are apples, bananas, oranges, and limes!" Ben says.

They go to the truck and take a lime each. They peel the lime and bite into it. They make funny faces and spit out the lime.

"I don't like it either! Let's go back to the swings!" Ben says.

"Hey, you kids! Why did you take my limes? Those are not for you! Those are for rich people who pay a lot of money for them!" he shouts.

Ben and Lily are scared. They jump off the swings and run away. They hide behind a tree.

"Sorry, mister, we didn't know!" Ben says.

"We just wanted to try them!" Lily says.

"Well, you should ask before you take things that are not yours! And don't ever take my limes again! They are too good for you!" the man says.

He gets back into his truck and drives away.

Ben and Lily are sad. They don't understand why the man was so mean. They don't think limes are good at all. They hug each other and go home. They decide to eat something sweet instead. They like cookies and ice cream better than limes.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big pile of waste near the swings. The waste is dull and smelly. Sara and Ben do not like the waste.

"Who put the waste here?" Sara asks. "It is bad for the park and the animals."

"I do not know," Ben says. "Maybe some people who do not care."

Sara and Ben want to help. They find some bags and gloves. They start to pick up the waste and put it in the bags. They work hard and fast.

Soon, a man comes to the park. He is the park keeper. He sees Sara and Ben and the bags of waste. He is happy and proud.

"Hello, Sara and Ben," he says. "You are doing a great job. Thank you for caring about the park and the animals."

He gives them some stickers and a hug. He takes the bags of waste to his truck. He waves to Sara and Ben as he drives away.

Sara and Ben wave back. They feel good and happy. They go back to the swings and have fun. They love the park and the animals.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They are happy.

But the sun is going down. It is time to go home. Tom and Anna say bye to each other.

"See you tomorrow, Anna!" Tom says.

"See you tomorrow, Tom!" Anna says.

Tom goes home with his mom. Anna goes home with her dad. They have dinner. They brush their teeth. They put on their pajamas.

Tom and Anna have a bag. The bag is big and soft. The bag is for sleeping. Tom and Anna love their bag.

Tom and Anna get into their bag. They hug their teddy bears. They close their eyes.

"Good night, Tom," Tom's mom says.

"Good night, Anna," Anna's dad says.

"Good night, mom. Good night, dad. I love you," Tom and Anna say.

Tom and Anna sleep. They dream of the park. They are good and happy.

Sara likes to collect rocks. She has many rocks of different colors and shapes. She keeps them in a big box in her room. She likes to look at them and touch them.

One day, she goes to the park with her mom and dad. She sees a big pile of rocks near the pond. She runs to the pile and starts to pick up the rocks. She finds a rock that is very rough and has many bumps. She likes it a lot.

"Look, mom, look, dad!" she says, holding the rock. "I found a new rock for my collection!"

Her mom and dad come to see the rock. Her dad smiles and says, "That's a very nice rock, Sara. Do you know what kind of rock it is?"

Sara shakes her head. She does not know.

Her dad says, "This is a rock from another nation. A nation is a big place where many people live. This rock came from a nation far away, across the sea. It is called a coral rock. It used to be part of a big, beautiful home for many fish and plants under the water. But the water got too warm and the home got sick and died. Then the waves and the wind broke the home into pieces and brought some of them here."

Sara feels sad for the fish and plants. She says, "I'm sorry for the home. It must have been very pretty."

Her mom says, "It was, Sara. But you can do something to help. You can take good care of this rock and remember the home it came from. You can also learn more about the other nations and the people and animals that live there. And you can be kind to the earth and the water, so they can stay healthy and happy."

Sara nods. She says, "I will, mom. I will, dad. Thank you for telling me about the rock and the nation. I will keep it in my box and look at it every day."

She hugs the rock and puts it in her pocket. She feels happy to have a new rock for her collection, and a new story to tell.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes the ball went too far and they had to run after it.

One time, the ball went over the fence and into the street. Lily and Ben were scared. They knew the street was dangerous and they should not go there. They saw a big car coming fast. The car did not see the ball.

"Look out, ball!" Lily shouted.

Ben was brave. He ran to the fence and reached for the ball. He wanted to save it. He stretched his arm and grabbed the ball just in time. The car zoomed past and missed the ball by a hair.

"Ben, you did it!" Lily said. She was happy and proud. She hugged Ben and gave him a high five. "You saved the ball! That was a success!"

Ben smiled. He was happy too. He felt a gentle scratch on his arm. He looked and saw a small cut from the fence. It hurt a little, but he did not cry.

"It's okay, Lily. It's just a scratch. I'm glad the ball is safe. It's our favorite ball."

Lily nodded. She took Ben's hand and they walked back to the park. They decided to play closer to the swings and slides. They did not want to lose their ball again. They had fun and laughed a lot. They were good friends.

Lily liked to number her toys. She had one doll, two cars, three balls, and four books. She put them in a line and counted them every day. She was very proud of her toys.

One day, her brother Max came into her room. He was bored and wanted to play. He saw Lily's toys and grabbed one of her cars. He said, "This is mine now. It is faster than yours."

Lily was angry. She said, "No, that is my car. Give it back. You have your own toys." She tried to take the car from Max, but he was stronger. He pushed her away and ran out of the room.

Lily followed him and saw him go to the kitchen. He took a match from the drawer and lit it. He said, "Look, I have a flame. It is bright and hot. I can burn your car with it."

Lily was scared. She said, "No, don't do that. You will hurt yourself and the car. The flame is dangerous. Put it out." She ran to get some water, but it was too late. Max threw the match on the car and it caught fire. He screamed and dropped the car. The flame grew bigger and bigger.

Lily poured the water on the fire and put it out. She was sad and angry. She said, "You are a bad brother. You ruined my car. It was cute and fun. Now it is black and broken. I don't want to play with you anymore." She picked up the car and went back to her room. She cried and hugged her doll.

Max felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was stupid and mean. I didn't mean to hurt you or your car. I just wanted to have some fun. Can you forgive me?" He knocked on her door and tried to make up with her. He gave her his favorite teddy bear and said, "This is for you. It is cute and soft. You can number it with your other toys. I love you, Lily. Please be my friend again."

One day, they have a contest to see who can build the highest structure. Lily starts with a red block, then adds a blue block, then a yellow block, and so on. Ben starts with a green block, then adds a green block, then another green block, and so on.

"Look at my structure!" Lily says. "It has many colors. It is pretty and fun."

"Look at my structure!" Ben says. "It has one color. It is strong and neat."

They keep adding blocks until their structures are very tall. They are both proud of their work.

But then, a gust of wind blows through the window. It makes Lily's structure wobble and fall. The blocks scatter on the floor.

"Oh no!" Lily cries. "My structure is gone!"

Ben laughs. He points at Lily's blocks and says, "Your structure is bad. It has too many colors. It is weak and messy."

Lily feels ashamed. She feels like crying. She does not like Ben's words.

But then, another gust of wind blows through the window. It makes Ben's structure sway and crash. The blocks tumble on the floor.

"Oh no!" Ben cries. "My structure is gone!"

Lily does not laugh. She does not point at Ben's blocks and say, "Your structure is bad. It has one color. It is boring and dull."

Lily feels sorry for Ben. She knows how he feels. She says, "I'm sorry your structure fell. It was not your fault. The wind was too strong."

Ben feels ashamed. He feels like saying sorry. He does not like his words.

He says, "I'm sorry I was mean. Your structure was not bad. It had many colors. It was pretty and fun."

Lily smiles. She says, "Thank you. Your structure was not bad either. It had one color. It was strong and neat."

They hug. They say, "Let's be friends."

They pick up the blocks and start to build again. This time, they match some blocks by color, and mix some blocks up. They make a new structure together. It has many colors and shapes. It is pretty and fun, strong and neat.

They are happy. They are not ashamed. They are proud of their work.

Tom and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, climb and slide. But they did not like the big boy who was mean to them. He would push them, take their toys and laugh at them. He had a whip that he made from a rope and a stick. He would whip the air and make a loud noise.

One day, Tom and Lily were sliding on the slide. They were having fun and giggling. But then they saw the big boy coming. He had his whip in his hand. He looked angry and mean. He said, "Get off the slide, you babies. It's my turn. I will whip you if you don't move."

Tom and Lily were scared. They did not want to get whipped. They tried to slide down quickly, but the big boy was faster. He grabbed Tom by his shirt and pulled him off the slide. He raised his whip and said, "Now you will learn your lesson, you crybaby."

But then something happened. A big dog came running from the other side of the park. It was a friendly and compassionate dog. It saw the big boy hurting Tom and did not like it. It barked loudly and ran towards the big boy. It jumped on him and knocked him down. It bit his whip and tore it apart. It licked Tom's face and wagged its tail.

The big boy was scared. He dropped his whip and ran away. He did not come back to the park. Tom and Lily were happy. They hugged the dog and thanked it. They named it Hero. They played with Hero on the slide and had more fun than ever. They made a new friend who was brave and kind. They learned that being mean is not good and being compassionate is better.

Sara and Tom were friends. They liked to play outside. One day, they went to the creek. The creek had water and rocks and fish. Sara and Tom wanted to catch fish.

"Look, Tom, a pretty fish!" Sara said. She pointed to a shiny fish in the water. She tried to grab it with her hand, but the fish was too fast. It swam away.

"Let me try, Sara," Tom said. He took a stick and poked the water. He hoped to hit the fish with the stick, but he missed. The fish was too smart. It hid under a rock.

Sara and Tom were sad. They wanted to catch a fish, but they could not. They sat on the bank and looked at the water.

"Maybe we should try something else," Sara said. "Maybe we can make a boat with leaves and sticks. Then we can sail on the creek."

"That sounds fun, Sara," Tom said. He smiled. He liked to make things. He and Sara started to look for leaves and sticks.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a dog. A big, black dog. It ran towards them, barking and growling. It wanted to chase them.

Sara and Tom were scared. They did not like the dog. They did not know the dog. They thought the dog would hurt them.

"Run, Sara, run!" Tom said. He grabbed Sara's hand and they ran away from the creek. They ran to their house. They ran to their mom.

"Mom, mom, help!" Sara and Tom said. They hugged their mom. They told her about the dog.

"Oh, my poor children," their mom said. She hugged them back. She kissed them. She said, "You are safe now. The dog can't get you here. I'm sorry you had to suffer. I'm sorry you couldn't catch a fish. But I'm glad you are okay. You are brave and smart and pretty. I love you."

Sara and Tom felt better. They loved their mom. They said, "We love you too, mom. Thank you for helping us. Can we have a cookie?"

Their mom smiled. She said, "Yes, you can have a cookie. And maybe tomorrow, we can go to the creek again. But this time, we will bring a net. And maybe we will catch a fish."

Lily and Ben were playing on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shells. They found many shells of different colors and shapes. Some were small and shiny, some were big and spiky, some were smooth and round.

"Look, Lily, I found a huge shell!" Ben said, holding up a shell that was bigger than his hand. "It has a zip on it!"

Lily ran over to see. She saw that the shell had a long line on it that looked like a zip. She wondered what was inside.

"Can we open it?" she asked.

Ben nodded. He tried to pull the zip, but it was very hard. He asked Lily to help him. They both pulled and pulled, but the zip did not move.

"Maybe it is stuck," Lily said.

"Maybe it is not a zip," Ben said.

They heard a noise from the shell. It sounded like a snore. They looked at each other and gasped.

"Maybe it is a sleeping animal!" Lily said.

They dropped the shell and ran away. They did not want to wake up the animal. They did not know what it was. Maybe it was a crab, or a turtle, or a monster.

They ran back to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a blanket. They told them about the huge shell with the zip and the noise.

Mom and dad smiled. They knew what it was. They took Lily and Ben back to the shell and showed them.

"It is not a zip, it is a hinge," mom said. "And it is not an animal, it is a clam."

She opened the shell gently and showed them the clam inside. It was soft and wet and had two eyes.

"It is not a monster, it is a friend," dad said. "It was sleeping because it was tired. It likes to live in the shell and filter the water."

Lily and Ben looked at the clam. They felt sorry for disturbing it. They said sorry to the clam and thanked it for letting them see it.

They put the shell back in the sand and covered it with some seaweed. They hoped the clam would have a good nap.

They learned something new that day. They learned that shells can have hinges, and clams can have shells, and zips can be hard to open. They also learned to be kind to the creatures of the sea. They had fun on the beach.

One day, they saw a big dog in the park. The dog was not friendly and barked very loud. Tim was scared and ran away, but Sam did not hear the dog. He stayed and played with his ball. The dog saw Sam and ran towards him. Sam did not see the dog.

Tim looked back and saw the dog chasing Sam. He felt bad for leaving his friend. He wanted to help Sam, but he did not know how. He could not use his voice to warn Sam, because Sam could not hear him. He could not use his hands to talk, because Sam could not see him. He had to think fast.

He saw a stick on the ground and picked it up. He threw the stick as hard as he could at the dog. The stick hit the dog on the nose and made it yelp. The dog stopped and ran away. "No, you can't," Sam said. "This is my car. I own it. It is rare. You can play with my other cars, but not this one."

"Fine, then I don't want to play with you at all," Tom said. "You are not a good friend. You are selfish."

Sam felt angry. He thought Tom was being rude. He did not care if Tom did not want to play with him. He had his rare car. He hugged it to his chest.

"Good, then go away," Sam said. "I don't need you. I have my car. It is better than you."

At the park, Lisa met a little puppy. After Lisa gave it some food, the puppy followed her back home.

It wasn't until Lisa and the puppy got back home that Lisa realized she had done something wrong. Her dad was angry and shouted at her.

"Lisa why did you go to the park without asking? Now, we have a puppy to look after," he said. Lisa felt so guilty that she started to cry.

Her mother then stepped in and said, "That's enough, dad. We can all take care of the puppy together. Let's go polish the fence and make it look nice so Lisa can be proud of it."

So, that's what they all did! They polished the fence and it sparkled in the sun. Lisa was so proud of what they had done that she vowed to never climb the fence again.

Once upon a time there was a rich farmer who lived near a lake. Every day he would lay down in the cool grass and watch the animals play in the sun.

One day, the farmer saw something moving in the lake. He sat up to get a closer look and he saw a big, round circle rolling across the top of the water. The farmer was very curious and he wanted to see what it was so he called to it.

"Hello, what are you doing in there?" the farmer asked.

The circle said, "I'm swimming! I'm a fish and I'm looking for food".

The farmer was surprised and he said, "Well, how exciting! Would you like to join me in the grass?".

The fish thought that sounded nice so the farmer lay down in the grass and the fish floated in a circle around him. The fish then told the farmer about the wonderful world of the lake and all the creatures that lived there. They talked for hours until the sun began to set and it was time for the fish to go home.

The farmer thanked the fish for all of her stories and said goodbye. As the fish swam away, the farmer lay back down and smiled as he watched the sun set. He now knew the rich world that lay inside the lake and it made him happy.

Startled, Bart looked around. Then he saw a little ladybug perched on a nearby flower. She was smiling.

"Spring is a great time for adventures," she said. "Come on, let's go explore!"

Bart's anxiety started to fade. Together, he and the ladybug crept through the lush green garden. They passed by bright yellow daisies and a sour-smelling orange tree.

Eventually, they reached a little pond. Bart went right in and splashed around. He took in the beauty of everything around him, and he forgot all about feeling anxious.

The ladybug and Bart stayed in the pond until the sun went down. When it was time to go, Bart felt happy and excited. He knew there were more adventures ahead.

"I know - a big screen and lots of seats!" Bailey said.

Bailey's mommy smiled and said, "Yes, but there's more. See those regular seats? Those are for us!"

Bailey said, "Yay!" She knew that meant they could watch the movie. 

So Bailey, her mommy and her daddy all settled into their regular seats together and watched the movie.  Bailey had the best day ever!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. She loved listening to her Uncle's stories.

One day, when she was only three years old, she asked her Uncle for a story.

He smiled and said, "Once upon a time there was a deep, dark forest."

Amy was very excited and asked, "What happened next, Uncle?"

Her Uncle smiled and continued. "In the middle of the forest was a big, tall tree with a room inside it."

Amy gasped in surprise. She asked, "What was in the room, Uncle?"

Uncle answered, "Well, it was full of shiny treasures and it was guarded by a very fierce dragon."

Amy's eyes sparkled as she asked, "How did the story end, Uncle?"

Uncle replied, "That is for you to find out, but I can tell you this much, a brave knight saved the day!"

At that Amy smiled and hugged her Uncle and said, "I love your stories!"

As Tim sat at his desk, he noticed something unusual. There was a tiny bug crawling across the surface. Tim said, "Mom, look! There's an unusual bug on my desk!" His mom came over and they both looked at the bug. They decided to catch it and take it outside to let it go. Tim was happy that his desk was clean and he could use it to draw and play again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and fly her kite. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. She brought her kite with her.

Lily tried to fly her kite, but it was too heavy. "Mommy, my kite is too heavy," Lily said. "Can you help me?"

"Sure, Lily. Let's hang the kite up in the tree," said her mommy. They hung the kite up in the tree so it could rest.

After a while, the wind picked up and Lily's kite flew high in the sky. "Look, Mommy! My kite is flying!" Lily shouted with joy.

"I see it, Lily. You did a great job hanging it up earlier," said her mommy.

Lily smiled and played with her kite all day long. She was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck who loved to play by the river. Every day, the little duck would waddle along the riverbank and quack with joy. One day, the little duck saw a big, strong ant pushing a big, heavy seed across the bridge.

The little duck was fascinated by the ant's persistent effort to push the seed across the bridge. The duck watched as the ant slowly but surely made its way across the bridge. The little duck quacked in admiration and decided to follow the ant.

But as the little duck got to the middle of the bridge, it felt a sudden gust of wind. The wind was so strong that it pushed the little duck off the bridge and into the river. The little duck tried to swim, but the current was too strong. The little duck was swept away, and it never saw the ant again.

Moral of the story: Sometimes, even the most persistent efforts can be undone by unexpected events.

Lily understood and let the bug go. She watched it fly away and felt happy knowing that it was free and safe. From that day on, she continued to explore the outdoors and find other interesting bugs to observe, but she always made sure to permit them to live in their natural habitat.

Her mom replied, "It's a surprise, Lily. You have to wait and see."

Lily was excited and couldn't wait for the pie. When the pie was ready, her mom brought it to the table. It was a blueberry pie. Lily took a bite and didn't like it. She started to cry.

Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. We can make apple pie next time. Remember, trying something different can be fun, but it's okay if you don't like it." From that day on, Lily learned to be more open-minded and willing to try new things.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie had a tall trunk that she used to pick up food and water. One day, Ellie was walking in the forest when she heard a little bird chirping. 

"Hello little birdie," Ellie said. "Why are you chirping so loudly?"

"I lost my nest," replied the birdie. "I need a tall tree to build a new one."

Ellie thought for a moment and then said, "I have an idea! You can build your nest in my trunk. It's tall enough and you'll be safe from any predators."

The little birdie was so happy and built a cozy nest in Ellie's trunk. From that day on, Ellie and the little birdie became the best of friends. They would often talk and play together, and Ellie loved hearing the birdie's sweet chirping.

Her grandma frowned and said, "I know, Lily. It's a bad habit and it's spoiled my health." 

Lily felt sad for her grandma and said, "I don't want you to be sick. Please stop smoking." 

Her grandma smiled and said, "You're right, Lily. I will try to quit smoking for you." 

From that day on, Lily's grandma stopped smoking and they both lived happily ever after.

Max thought about it and realized that Lily was right. He apologized for being envious and they both enjoyed their apples together. From that day on, Max learned the value of sharing and never wanted to be greedy again.

The moral of the story is that sharing is important and it makes us happy. We should always try to share with others, just like Lily did with Max. And don't forget to pack an extra apple for your friend!

Lily was a little girl who liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers, the bugs and the birds. One day, she saw something new on a leaf. It was small and round and green. She wondered what it was.

She picked up the leaf and took it to her mom. "Mom, what is this?" she asked, pointing at the green thing.

Mom looked at the leaf and smiled. "That is a cell, Lily. A cell is a very tiny part of a living thing. This cell is from a plant. Plants have green cells that help them make food from the sun."

Lily was amazed. She wanted to see more cells. "Can I see cells from other things, Mom?" she asked.

Mom nodded. "Yes, you can. But you need a special tool called a microscope. A microscope can make things look bigger, so you can see the cells. Do you want to try?"

Lily was excited. She said yes. Mom took her to the study, where she had a microscope. She put a drop of water on a slide and put it under the microscope. She let Lily look through the eyepiece.

Lily gasped. She saw many different shapes and colors. Some were moving, some were still. Some were round, some were long. Some were clear, some were red. "What are these, Mom?" she asked.

Mom explained. "These are cells from different living things in the water. Some are from animals, some are from plants, some are from other things. They all have different jobs and functions. They are amazing, aren't they?"

Lily nodded. She was amazed. She wondered how many cells there were in the world. She wondered how many cells she had in her body. She wondered how cells worked together to make life. She wanted to learn more. She thanked Mom for showing her the microscope. She decided to keep the leaf with the green cell as a souvenir. She thought it was beautiful.

The little girl smiled. She didn't feel so scared anymore.

The skull and the little girl became good friends. They had lots of fun together, exploring all the spooky places in the woods.

The moral of the story is: Respect nature and listen to your siblings.

One day, they go to the museum with Mom. They see many things. They see dinosaurs, paintings, and rocks. They are happy and curious.

They come to a room with a big glass case. Inside the case, there is a brain. It is gray and wrinkly. It has wires and tubes. Lily and Ben are amazed.

"Mom, what is that?" Lily asks.

"That is a brain, Lily. It is the most incredible part of your body. It helps you think, feel, remember, and imagine. It is very special," Mom says.

"Wow, a brain! Can I touch it?" Ben asks.

"No, Ben. You cannot touch it. It is very delicate. But you can observe it. You can see how it works. Look, there are lights and sounds. They show what the brain does," Mom says.

Lily and Ben observe the brain. They see the lights and hear the sounds. They learn about the brain. They think it is incredible. They want to have a brain like that. They smile and hug Mom. They love to observe.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and balls. But sometimes they fight over toys. They want the same toy and do not share.

One day, Mom is sick. She has a bad cough and a fever. She needs to rest and take pills. Dad tells Tom and Sam to be quiet and help Mom.

Tom and Sam want to help Mom. But they also want to play. They see a big box of toys in the living room. They run to the box and start to grab toys.

Tom sees a red car. He likes red cars. He takes the car and says, "This is mine!"

Sam sees a blue ball. He likes blue balls. He takes the ball and says, "This is mine!"

But then they see a yellow truck. They both like yellow trucks. They both want the truck. They start to pull the truck and shout, "This is mine! This is mine!"

Mom hears the noise. She feels worse. She calls Dad and says, "Please hurry! I need a pill and some water. And please make Tom and Sam stop fighting. They are making me sicker."

Dad hears Mom. He hurries to the bedroom. He gives Mom a pill and some water. He kisses Mom and says, "I hope you feel better soon. I love you."

Then he hurries to the living room. He sees Tom and Sam fighting over the truck. He is angry. He says, "Stop it! You are being bad boys. You are making Mom sicker. You should be helping Mom, not fighting over toys. You should be sharing, not being jealous. You should be sorry, not selfish."

Tom and Sam hear Dad. They feel ashamed. They drop the truck and say, "We are sorry, Dad. We are sorry, Mom. We love you. We want to help you. We will share and be nice."

Dad smiles and says, "That's good. I'm proud of you. Now, let's put away the toys and make Mom a card. She will be happy to see that you care."

Tom and Sam nod and say, "Yes, Dad. Let's do that."

They put away the toys and make Mom a card. They draw hearts and flowers and write, "We love you, Mom. Get well soon."

They give the card to Mom. Mom smiles and says, "Thank you, Tom and Sam. You are good boys. I love you. You make me feel better."

Tom and Sam hug Mom and say, "You're welcome, Mom. We love you. You make us happy."

The end.

Moral: Fighting over toys is bad. Sharing and caring is good. Helping others is better.

One day, she saw a bird on the window. The bird was small and brown, with a yellow beak. It sang a pretty song. Lily thought the bird was cute and wanted to talk to it. She jumped on the window and said, "Hello, bird. Do you want to be my friend?"

The bird was scared and flew away. Lily was sad and wondered why the bird did not like her. She lay on the couch and sighed.

The kind lady saw Lily and felt sorry for her. She said, "Lily, I know you want a friend, but you cannot be friends with a bird. Birds are afraid of cats, because cats sometimes chase and hurt them. You need to find a friend who is like you, who likes to play and run and cuddle."

Lily looked at the lady and nodded. She understood that she had to be careful and respectful of other animals. She thanked the lady and gave her a lick.

Lily said, "My name is Lily. What is yours?"

Lily said, "Yes, we can. Come out of the box and let's have fun."

The lady opened the box and let Max out. Lily and Max ran and played and cuddled. They were very happy and became the best of friends. The lady smiled and watched them. She was glad that she had given Lily a friend who was like her.

The moral of the story is: You can make friends with others who are like you and who share your interests. You should also be respectful and careful of those who are different from you and who may be afraid of you.

Lily and Max were playing with their toy boats in the bathtub. They pretended they were explorers sailing to different islands. They had a map that showed them where to go.

"Look, Max, this is the island of the dinosaurs!" Lily said, pointing to a green spot on the map. "Let's go there and see what we can find."

"Okay, Lily, but be careful. Dinosaurs are big and scary. Maybe they will roar at us." Max said, following her with his boat.

They moved their boats closer to the edge of the bathtub, where they had placed some plastic plants and rocks to make the island. They used their fingers to make their boats land on the shore.

"Wow, this island is mysterious. I wonder if there are any dinosaurs hiding here." Lily said, looking around.

"Shh, Lily, I hear something. It sounds like a dinosaur." Max said, holding his boat.

They saw a shadow moving behind the plants. They gasped and held their breath. Then, a small dinosaur toy popped out and displayed its teeth and claws. It was their brother Jake, who had sneaked into the bathroom and wanted to scare them.

"Roar! I am the king of the dinosaurs! You are my lunch!" Jake said, making his toy attack their boats.

"Ah! Jake, you are mean! Go away!" Lily said, pushing his toy away.

"Ha ha, I got you! You were so scared!" Jake said, laughing.

"No, we were not scared. We were brave explorers. You are a silly dinosaur." Max said, splashing water at him.

"Stop it, you three! You are making a mess! Time to get out of the bathtub!" their mom said, coming into the bathroom.

"Okay, mom. But can we play with the islands again tomorrow?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey. But only if you clean up your toys and dry yourselves." their mom said.

"Okay, mom. We will. We love the islands. They are fun and mysterious." Lily and Max said.

They got out of the bathtub and wrapped themselves in towels. They hugged their mom and their brother and went to their room. They put their map and their boats on their shelf and smiled. They had a great adventure on the island of the dinosaurs.

"Come on, let's go," Lily says. "We have to get our bikes. Hurry!"

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to eat toast with jam for breakfast. Mom makes two pieces of toast and puts them on a plate. She gives them a knife and a jar of jam.

"Here you go, kids. Spread some jam on your toast and enjoy. But don't make a mess, please," Mom says.

Anna and Ben say thank you and start to spread jam on their toast. Anna likes a lot of jam, so she spreads it thick and sticky. Ben likes a little jam, so he spreads it thin and smooth. They finish their first pieces and reach for the second ones.

But there is a problem. There is only a little jam left in the jar. Not enough for both of them.

"Hey, that's not fair! I want more jam!" Anna says.

"No, I want more jam! You already had too much!" Ben says.

They start to argue and pull the jar and the knife. The jar falls on the floor and breaks. The jam spills everywhere. Mom hears the noise and comes back to the kitchen.

"Oh no! What have you done?" Mom says. "Look at this mess! You wasted the jam and broke the jar! And you didn't even finish your toast!"

Anna and Ben feel bad. They know they were wrong. They say sorry to Mom and to each other.

"Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Ben. I was greedy and rude," Anna says.

"Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Anna. I was mean and selfish," Ben says.

Mom sighs and hugs them. She is not happy, but she loves them.

"It's okay, kids. I forgive you. But you have to learn to share and be polite. And you have to help me clean up this mess. And no more jam for today. Maybe tomorrow we can have some honey. It's also tasty," Mom says.

Anna and Ben nod and smile. They help Mom clean up the kitchen. They finish their toast and drink some milk. They hug Mom and say thank you. They learn their lesson and promise to do better. They love Mom and each other.

"See, Tom. The alligator is happy. It likes the ball. Come and play with us," Sara says.

Tom is curious. He goes back to the pond. He pushes the car to the alligator. The alligator pushes the car back with its nose. It makes another loud noise. Tom thinks it is smiling.

"Wow, Sara. You are right. The alligator is not bad. It is kind. It likes the car. This is fun," Tom says.

Sara and Tom play with the alligator for a long time. They use the ball and the car. They are kind friends. The alligator is kind too. It is not lonely anymore. They are happy.

Tom came down the hill. He saw Lily eating pie. He wanted some too. He said, "Can I have some pie, please?" The nice lady looked at him. She said, "Did you push Lily down the hill?" Tom nodded. He was sorry. He said, "I am sorry. I was grumpy. I will not do it again." The nice lady said, "That is good. You should be nice to your friend. You can have some pie too. But you have to say sorry to Lily first." Tom said sorry to Lily. Lily said it was okay. They hugged. They shared the pie. They were happy.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They swing, slide and run. They are very jolly.

One day, Lily sees a big dog. The dog is barking and running. Lily is scared. She runs to Tom and holds his hand.

"Tom, I don't like the dog. He is loud and fast. He might bite us," Lily says.

Tom looks at the dog. He is not scared. He likes dogs. He knows the dog is just playing.

"Lily, don't worry. The dog is nice. He just wants to have fun. He won't hurt us," Tom says.

He lets go of Lily's hand and walks to the dog. He smiles and says, "Hello, dog. What is your name?"

The dog stops barking and wags his tail. He licks Tom's face. Tom laughs and pets the dog.

Lily sees that the dog is friendly. She feels better. She walks to Tom and the dog. She touches the dog's fur. It is soft and warm.

"Hello, dog. I'm Lily. You are cute," Lily says.

The dog wags his tail more. He likes Lily and Tom. He wants to play with them.

Lily and Tom are happy. They play with the dog. They throw a ball and the dog fetches it. They hug the dog and the dog kisses them.

They are very jolly. They care for the dog and the dog cares for them. They are friends.

"Me too," Sue says. "But this melon is weird. Why does it have spots?"

They go closer to the melon. They want to touch it. But the melon is not a melon. It is a ball. A big ball with a melon picture on it.

"Surprise!" a voice says. It is Ben, their other friend. He is hiding behind a tree. He has a big smile. He likes to make jokes.

"Ben, you are silly!" Tom says. "This is not a melon. This is a ball. You tricked us!"

"Ha ha, I did!" Ben says. "Do you want to play with the ball?"

"Yes, we do!" Tom and Sue say. They are not mad. They like to play with Ben.

They take the ball and run to the grass. They throw the ball and catch it. They have fun. They laugh and giggle. They forget about the weird melon. They are happy.

A few days later, Benny saw a dead flower. He knew that he couldn't skip past it without doing something. So, he dug a little hole and planted the flower, hoping it would grow again. Benny felt happy knowing that he had helped the flower come back to life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a frog near a pond. The frog was green and had big eyes.

Lily said, "Hello Mr. Frog, what are you doing here?" The frog replied, "I am waiting for my friend to call me." Lily thought the frog was very nosy because he was always asking about his friend.

Suddenly, the frog's phone rang. He said, "Excuse me, Lily, I have to answer this call." The frog hopped away to answer the phone. Lily watched as the frog talked on the phone for a long time.

After the call, the frog came back and said, "My friend is coming to visit me. Thank you for keeping me company, Lily." Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mr. Frog. Have a nice day!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went for a walk in the forest with her mommy. They saw many trees and flowers, but what caught Lily's eye was a vine. It was long and green, and she had never seen anything like it before.

"Mommy, look at that vine! It's so unique," said Lily.

"Yes, it is. Do you want to touch it?" asked her mommy.

Lily reached out and touched the vine. It felt rough and bumpy. "I see why it's so unique now," she said.

As they continued their walk, they heard a bird singing in the trees. "I see the bird, mommy!" exclaimed Lily.

"That's right, Lily. It's a beautiful day to be outside and see all the wonderful things nature has to offer," said her mommy.

Lily smiled and continued to enjoy their walk in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a big black bird called a raven. The raven lived in a tall tree in a forest. One day, the raven felt very sleepy and decided to take a nap on a branch.

As the raven slept, the tree began to tremble. The raven woke up and looked around. It saw a little mouse running up the tree. The mouse was scared and shaking, making the tree tremble.

The raven felt sorry for the little mouse and decided to help. It flew down to the ground and found some cheese to give to the mouse. The mouse was very happy and stopped trembling. From that day on, the raven and the mouse became good friends and would often play together in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat delicious apples from her grandpa's tree. One day, she noticed that her grandpa's hair was turning white. She asked him why his hair was changing color. 

Grandpa explained that when people get older, their hair and skin change. They lose their youth, but gain wisdom and experience. Lily didn't understand everything grandpa said, but she knew that she loved him no matter what. 

As they sat together eating their delicious apples, Lily thought about how lucky she was to have such a wonderful grandpa. She didn't care about his hair or his age, she just loved spending time with him.

Lily learned that sometimes we need to be patient and let things happen naturally, instead of trying to force them. And that's why it's important to wait for your wobbly tooth to fall out on its own.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sail on her boat with her teddy bear, Mr. Snuggles. "Yes, it is," replied Mr. Snuggles, "and it looks so sweet, like a giant cookie in the sky." Lily giggled and agreed.

As they continued to sail, Lily noticed something strange. "Mr. Snuggles, do you see that over there?" she asked, pointing to a dark shape in the water. "Yes, I do," said Mr. Snuggles, "it looks like a big fish." Suddenly, the fish jumped out of the water and onto their boat! "Oh no!" cried Lily, "what are we going to do?" Mr. Snuggles had an idea. "Let's give the fish a sweet cookie," he suggested. Lily quickly grabbed a cookie from her bag and gave it to the fish. The fish happily ate the cookie and then swam away, leaving Lily and Mr. Snuggles safe on their boat.

From then on, Lily always brought sweet cookies on her sailing adventures, just in case they met any more hungry fish. And every time they looked up at the moon, they remembered their sweet adventure on the water.

But Anna soon found out the maze was much bigger than it seemed. She got lost and couldn't find her way out. After a while, Anna became very scared. Then she heard her mum's voice.

Her mum was standing at the entrance, insisting that Anna come out. But Anna wanted to stay. She wanted to solve the maze and be brave. So her mum made a deal: if Anna came out now, she would come back again soon with Anna's dad and they would solve the maze together.

Anna accepted the deal. She followed her mum out of the maze. Then, a few days later, she returned with her dad who had a mild look on his face. Together, they ran around the maze, laughing and finding their way out. Anna felt so proud and happy that she had insisted on solving the maze!

A battery sat in a small room, alone. Then a graceful woman arrived - she was excited to see it. She picked up the battery, feeling its weight in her hands, and then placed it on the table.

The battery seemed to know what was about to happen, and it started bouncing up and down. The woman chuckled happily, and soon the whole room was filled with the sound of her joy.

The woman then reached for a small box, opening its lid. She carefully placed the battery inside, before connecting a few wires. Suddenly, the room was illuminated with bright lights.

The woman was delighted. It felt as though the simple battery had given her an unexpected gift of light. She thanked the battery, then ran out of the room in excitement.

The battery watched its new friend leave, happy to have had the chance to make someone smile. It then gently rested in its new home, content and graceful.

Maya thanked the jailer and vowed never to make that mistake again. From then on, she only picked flowers from her own garden.

One night, they found a big box of glow sticks in the garage. They were so happy and excited. They took the box to their room and opened it. There were many colors and shapes of glow sticks. They wanted to try them all.

They turned off the light and started to crack and shake the glow sticks. They made bracelets and necklaces and crowns and swords. They glowed like rainbows in the dark. They laughed and played and had fun.

"Look, Lily, I'm a famous knight!" Ben said, holding a glow stick sword. "I can fight dragons and monsters!"

"And I'm a famous princess!" Lily said, wearing a glow stick crown. "I can make wishes and magic!"

They pretended to go on adventures and save the world. They were having so much fun that they did not hear their mom calling them for dinner.

But then, something strange happened. One of the glow sticks started to make a hissing sound. It was a big one, shaped like a rocket. Ben had found it in the bottom of the box. He thought it was cool and wanted to see how it glowed.

He cracked it and shook it, but it did not glow. It only hissed louder and louder. Then, it burst open with a loud bang. A spray of sparks flew out of it and hit the curtains. The curtains caught fire and started to burn.

Lily and Ben screamed and ran out of the room. They saw their mom in the hallway. She smelled the smoke and saw the fire. She grabbed them and took them outside. She called the firemen to come and put out the fire.

Lily and Ben were scared and sorry. They did not know the glow stick was dangerous. They did not mean to start a fire. They hugged their mom and cried.

The firemen came and put out the fire. They checked the house and said it was safe. They asked Lily and Ben what happened. They told them about the glow sticks and the rocket.

The firemen looked at the box of glow sticks. They saw a label on it. It said: "Warning: Not for children. For professional use only. Contains flammable material. Do not crack or shake. Do not expose to heat or flame."

The firemen shook their heads and said: "These are not glow sticks. These are fireworks. They are very dangerous. You should never play with them. You are lucky you did not get hurt."

Lily and Ben felt ashamed and learned a lesson. They said they were sorry and thanked the firemen. They promised to never play with fireworks again. They also promised to listen to their mom and come to dinner when she called.

Their mom hugged them and said she loved them. She said she was glad they were safe. She said they could still play with glow sticks, but only the safe ones. She said she would buy them some new ones tomorrow.

Lily and Ben smiled and said they loved her too. They said they would be more careful and responsible. They said they still liked to pretend they were famous, but they did not need fireworks to do that. They said they could use their imagination and have fun.

The horse did not answer. He bent his head and ate some grass. Anna tried to climb on his back, but she was too small. She pulled his mane, but he did not move. She said, please, horse, let me ride you. I will be very gentle.

The horse did not like Anna pulling his mane. He shook his head and snorted. He moved away from Anna. Anna followed him. She said, don't go, horse, I want to be your friend.

The horse did not want to be Anna's friend. He wanted to be alone. He ran to the other side of the field. Anna ran after him. She said, wait, horse, wait.

The horse did not wait. He saw a gap in the fence. He jumped over it and ran to the road. Anna saw him jump and said, wow, horse, you can jump very high.

But the road was not safe. There were cars and trucks and bikes. The horse did not know about them. He was scared. He ran into the road and made a loud noise.

Anna saw the horse run into the road. She was scared too. She said, no, horse, no. Come back, horse, come back.

Ben heard Anna and the horse. He ran to the field and saw what happened. He was angry and worried. He said, Anna, what did you do? Why did you bother my horse? He is not harmless. He is dangerous. You could have hurt him and yourself.

Anna cried. She said, I'm sorry, Ben. I just wanted to ride your horse. He is so big and brown and fast. I did not mean to make him jump and run.

Ben sighed. He said, I know, Anna. But you have to listen to me. My horse is not for little girls. He is for big boys. You have to wait until you are bigger and stronger. Then you can ride a horse.

Anna nodded. She said, okay, Ben. I will wait. But can I still look at your horse? He is very pretty.

Ben smiled. He said, yes, Anna. You can look at my horse. But only from the fence. And only when I am with you.

Anna smiled too. She said, thank you, Ben. You are a good brother.

Ben hugged Anna. He said, you are welcome, Anna. You are a good sister.

They walked to the road and found the horse. He was not hurt. He was just scared. Ben calmed him down and led him back to the field. Anna said, hello, horse. I'm sorry I scared you. You are very brave.

The horse looked at Anna and made a noise. He said, hello, Anna. I'm sorry I ran away. You are very kind.

Anna and Ben laughed. They said, horse, you can talk?

The horse laughed too. He said, no, I can't. I'm just joking.

There was a king who liked to have many things. He had a big castle, a lot of gold, and many clothes. He was not happy, though. He always wanted more and more. He did not care about his people, who were poor and hungry.

One day, a man came to the castle. He said he was a traveler, and he had a gift for the king. The king was curious. He told his guards to bring the man to him. The man had a small box in his hand. He opened it and showed the king what was inside.

It was a ring. It was very shiny and had a red stone. The king liked shiny things. He wanted the ring. He asked the man how much he wanted for it. The man said he did not want money. He said he only wanted the king to be humble and kind.

The king laughed. He thought the man was silly. He said he did not need to be humble and kind. He said he was the king, and he could do whatever he wanted. He snatched the ring from the man and put it on his finger.

But as soon as he did, something strange happened. The ring was not a normal ring. It was a magic ring. It made the king shrink and shrink, until he was as small as a mouse. The man smiled. He said he was not a traveler, but a wizard. He said he wanted to teach the king a lesson. He said he hoped the king would learn to be humble and kind, or he would stay small forever.

The king was scared. He realized he had been foolish and greedy. He begged the man to make him big again. He said he would change his ways and help his people. The man said he would give the king a chance. He said he would make him big again, but only if he did three good deeds for his people. He said he would watch the king and see if he was telling the truth.

The king agreed. He took off the ring and gave it back to the man. The man said he would keep the ring until the king did his good deeds. He said he would come back in a week and see if the king had kept his promise. He left the castle and disappeared.

The king was ashamed. He realized he had been a bad king. He decided to do his best to be humble and kind. He started to share his things with his people. He gave them food and clothes and money. He listened to their problems and helped them. He made them happy.

The people were surprised. They did not know what had happened to the king. They thought he had changed his heart. They were grateful and loyal. They loved the king.

A week later, the man came back. He saw that the king had done his good deeds. He was proud of the king. He said he had passed the test. He gave the king the ring and said he could keep it. He said it was a reminder of his lesson. He said he hoped the king would always be humble and kind.

The king thanked the man. He said he had learned his lesson. He said he would always be humble and kind. He said he did not need the ring anymore. He said he would give it to someone who needed it more. He said he was happy.

The man smiled. He said he was glad. He said he had one more gift for the king. He said he would make the ring a normal ring. He said it would not make the king shrink anymore. He said it would only make the king happy.

He waved his hand and said a magic word. The ring changed. It was not shiny anymore. It was dull and plain. But it had a new word on it. It said "humble". The king looked at the ring. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He put the ring on his finger. He felt happy.

The man said goodbye to the king. He said he hoped the king would always be happy. He said he hoped the king would always be humble and kind. He left the castle and disappeared.

The king lived happily ever after. He was a good king. He was humble and kind. He loved his people and they loved him. He never forgot his lesson. He never forgot his ring. He never forgot the man. He was happy.

Suddenly, a kind lady came and saw the two birds fighting over the nest. She took out a stamp and stamped a piece of paper to make a new home for Tweet. The new home was perfect for Tweet and he was very happy. From that day on, Tweet learned that it's always better to share and not be selfish.

It had fallen off the hanger and onto the floor. Timmy got up and picked up his shirt. He put it back on the hanger and made sure it was shut tight. Then he went back to bed and fell fast asleep again.

"Okay, bye, elephant," Tom said. "We hope you find your friends soon."

"Bye, Lily and Tom," the elephant said. "Thank you for playing with me. You are very kind and brave."

Lily and Tom waved goodbye to the elephant. They walked home, holding hands. They told their parents about their unusual adventure in the park. They never forgot the elephant who sneezed very loud.

They sailed back to the pier and tied their boat again. They were very happy and proud of their work. They hugged each other and said, "We are the best sailors ever!"

The end.

Lily and Tom were twins who lived on a big ranch with their mom and dad. They liked to play with the horses and cows and dogs. One day, they decided to explore the ranch and see what they could find.

They walked and walked until they saw a fence with a sign that said "Do not part". They were curious and wanted to see what was behind the fence. They looked around and did not see anyone. They thought it was a secret place.

They pushed the fence and made a hole. They crawled through the hole and entered a field with many flowers and trees. They saw a pond with ducks and frogs. They ran and laughed and picked some flowers.

They did not know that the field belonged to Mr. Brown, the neighbor who did not like children. He was very mean and angry. He saw them from his window and grabbed his gun. He ran outside and shouted at them.

"Hey, you little brats! What are you doing on my land? Get out of here or I'll shoot you!"

Lily and Tom were very scared and dropped the flowers. They tried to run back to the fence, but Mr. Brown was faster. He caught them and pointed his gun at them. He said he was going to teach them a lesson.

Lily and Tom cried and begged for mercy. They said they were sorry and did not know it was his land. They said they just wanted to have fun and see the pond. They said they would never part the fence again.

But Mr. Brown did not listen. He was very cruel and did not care. He pulled the trigger and shot them. Lily and Tom fell to the ground and did not move. They were dead.

Mr. Brown smiled and threw their bodies into the pond. He said he hated children and did not want them on his land. He fixed the fence and went back to his house.

The end.
