Tim saw that Spot was feeling left out. He didn't want his toy dog to be sad. So, Tim found a way to play with both the pot and Spot. He put Spot in the pot and pushed it around like a little car. Spot was happy again, and they all played together.

One day, a boy named Tim found a knife in the kitchen. He knew it was not a toy, so he decided to bury it in the garden. He took the knife outside and dug a small hole with his hands. Then, he put the knife into the hole and covered it with dirt.

Later, Tim's mom came outside and saw the hole. She asked, "Tim, what did you bury here?" Tim replied, "I buried a knife, Mom. I knew it was not for playing, so I hid it." His mom smiled and said, "You are successful in keeping us safe, Tim. Good job!"

From that day on, Tim felt proud of his choice to bury the knife. He knew he had done the right thing to keep his family safe. And every time he walked by the spot in the garden, he remembered how he was successful in protecting the ones he loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little train named Timmy. Timmy was a very creative train. He liked to make new tracks in the land. One day, Timmy wanted to make a big track that went all around the big hill.

Timmy worked hard every day. He made the track go up, down, and all around. It was not easy, but Timmy did not give up. He knew he had to manage his time well to finish the big track.

One day, when the track was almost done, Timmy saw a big storm coming. Timmy knew that the storm could break his track. He worked very fast to finish the track. Just as the storm came, Timmy finished the track. The storm did not break the track, and Timmy was very happy. His hard work and creative track made everyone in the land very proud.

Tim went outside and started to build his own big, icy snowman. He made the snowman look like the one in his favorite video. Tim played with his snowman all day and had so much fun. When it was time to go inside, he said, "Please, snowman, be my friend forever." And the snowman smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved ice cream, especially when it was so cold that it made her teeth hurt. One day, Lily was eating her ice cream with a spoon when she dropped the spoon on the ground. She tried to pick it up, but it was too icy and slippery. 

Lily's mommy came to help her and saw the problem. She told Lily that they needed to solve the problem of the icy spoon. They went inside and put the spoon in some warm water to make it less icy. Then, Lily could use the spoon again to eat her yummy ice cream. 

From that day on, Lily was always careful not to drop her spoon on the ground. And if it ever got too icy again, she knew how to solve the problem. The end.

Tweety was scared of Biggie at first because he looked very different from him. But Biggie was nice and wanted to help Tweety. "Let's complete a puzzle together!" said Biggie. Tweety was excited and they started working on a puzzle. 

As they were putting the puzzle pieces together, Tweety noticed that Biggie's steel feathers were getting rustier and rustier. "Are you okay, Biggie?" asked Tweety. "I'm okay, Tweety. I just need some oil to make me shiny again," replied Biggie. 

Tweety remembered seeing a can of oil in the park and went to get it for Biggie. When Tweety came back with the oil, Biggie was as good as new. "Thank you, Tweety. You're a great friend," said Biggie. Tweety was happy to have made a new friend and they continued to complete puzzles together.

The squirrel didn't answer. Instead, it started to run away. The little girl went after it and followed it into an unknown part of the woods. She kept going and going until she reached a little house. The squirrel stopped at the house and seemed to wait for the little girl.

The little girl slowly opened the door. Inside, she saw what the squirrel was looking for: nuts and berries! The squirrel had found a secret stash of food! The little girl smiled and thanked the squirrel for showing her the way. Then the two of them ran off into the woods together.

Lily took the bottle and poured some ink on another paper. She used her finger to draw a flower.

Mommy woke up. She smelled something spicy. She went to the kitchen. She saw the ink on the floor and on the papers. She saw Lily and Max with ink on their hands and faces.

"What are you doing?" she asked.

Lily and Max looked at Mommy. They felt scared.

"We are sorry, Mommy," they said. "We wanted to make a picture for you."

Mommy was not happy. She was angry. She took the bottle and the papers. She threw them in the trash.

"Mom, what is that?" Lily pointed to the fruit.

"That is an avocado. It is good for you, but you have to work hard to get it." Mom said.

"How do we work hard?" Max asked.

"You have to climb the tree, pick the avocado, and cut it open. Then you can eat it with some salt and lemon." Mom explained.

Lily and Max decided to try. They climbed the tree, but it was not easy. The branches were slippery and the leaves were scratchy. They reached the avocado, but it was not ripe. It was hard and bitter. They cut it open, but it was not creamy. It was brown and rotten. They tasted it, but it was not good. It was terrible.

"Yuck!" Lily spat out the avocado.

"Blech!" Max did the same.

They ran back to their mom, crying and rubbing their tongues.

"Mom, the avocado was terrible! It made us sick!" Lily complained.

"Mom, we worked hard, but we got nothing!" Max whined.

Mom hugged them and gave them some water. She said, "I'm sorry, my loves. Sometimes, working hard is not enough. You also have to work smart. You have to know when the avocado is ready, how to pick it, and how to store it. Otherwise, you will waste your time and energy, and end up with something terrible."

Lily and Max nodded. They learned their lesson. They decided to wait for mom to help them with the avocado next time. They also decided to play with something else in the garden. They found some flowers, some rocks, and some bugs. They had fun, and they did not get sick.

The moral of the story is: Working hard is not enough. You also have to work smart.

They tried to make a snowman with the wet salt, but it was too heavy and fell apart.

"This is a bad idea," Ben said. "Let's clean up before Mom sees."

They hoped Mom would not be mad at them. They used a towel to wipe the table and their hands. They put the jar of salt back on the shelf. They threw the towel in the trash.

They ran to their room and played with their toys. They did not want to play with salt again. It was too weird.

One day, Lily and her mom go to the park. Lily brings Star with her. She sees a big pony in a field. The pony is brown and has a long mane. Lily wants to pet the pony. She asks her mom, "Can I go to the pony, please?"

Mom says, "Yes, but be careful. The pony might be scared of you. And it is very hot today. The pony might be thirsty. Do you have some water for the pony?"

Lily nods. She has a bottle of water in her backpack. She takes it out and walks to the pony. She says, "Hello, pony. I am Lily. This is Star. She is my toy pony. Do you want some water?"

The pony looks at Lily and Star. He sniffs the water bottle. He nods his head. He is thirsty. Lily gives him some water. He drinks it and makes a happy sound. He licks Lily's hand. He likes Lily and Star.

Lily smiles. She pets the pony's mane. She says, "You are a nice pony. What is your name?"

The pony says, "I am Brownie. I live here with my friends. Do you want to meet them?"

Lily says, "Yes, please. I like ponies. Can Star come too?"

Brownie says, "Of course. Star is a cute pony. Come on, follow me."

Lily and Star follow Brownie to the other ponies. They have fun playing with them. Lily thinks this is the best day ever.

One day, his dad had to leave for work. He gave Tommy a hug and said, "Be good, Tommy. Don't play with my newspaper. It is difficult to find a new one. I need it for my job."

Tommy nodded and said, "Okay, dad. I love you. Bye-bye."

But after his dad left, Tommy saw the newspaper on the table. It looked so fun and interesting. He forgot what his dad said. He grabbed the newspaper and ran to his room.

He started to play with the newspaper. He folded it, cut it, and threw it. He made a hat, a boat, and a plane. He laughed and had a good time.

But then he heard his mom coming. She opened the door and saw the mess. She was very angry. She said, "Tommy, what did you do? You made a big mess with your dad's newspaper. He told you not to play with it. It is difficult to find a new one. He needs it for his job. You are in trouble, young man."

Tommy felt bad. He knew he did something wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I forgot. I just wanted to play. I love you. Please don't be mad."

His mom sighed and said, "I love you too, Tommy. But you have to listen to your dad and me. We tell you things for your own good. Now help me clean up this mess. And next time, find something else to play with."

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play together. One day, they found a shiny box in Anna's mom's room. The box had many pretty things inside, like rings and necklaces and earrings. They were jewelry.

"Wow, look at these!" Ben said. "Can we try them on?"

Anna nodded. She liked the jewelry too. She put on a ring and a necklace. Ben put on an earring and a bracelet. They looked at each other and laughed.

"You look funny!" Anna said.

"So do you!" Ben said.

They decided to play dress-up with the jewelry. They pretended to be a king and a queen. They bowed and danced and sang. They had a lot of fun.

Then, Anna had an idea. She leaned over and kissed Ben on the cheek.

"Yuck!" Ben said. He wiped his face with his hand. "Why did you do that?"

Anna felt ashamed. She did not know why she kissed Ben. She thought it was something that kings and queens did. She saw her mom and dad do it sometimes. She wanted to make Ben happy. But he did not like it. He looked angry and sad.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Anna said. "I just wanted to be nice. I didn't mean to make you mad."

Ben looked at Anna. He saw that she was sorry. He felt sorry too. He did not mean to hurt her feelings. He knew that she was his friend.

"It's okay, Anna," Ben said. "I'm not mad at you. I just don't like kisses. They are wet and sticky."

Anna smiled. She understood. She did not like kisses either. They were wet and sticky.

"Can we still be friends?" Anna asked.

"Of course we can," Ben said. "But no more kisses, okay?"

"Okay," Anna said. "No more kisses."

They hugged and said sorry to each other. Then they took off the jewelry and put it back in the box. They learned that not everyone likes the same things, and that they should respect each other's feelings. They also learned that they should not touch things that do not belong to them, because they might get in trouble. They were happy to be friends again.

Dad says, "You're welcome, Anna. I love you."

She saw Sam running towards her with tears in his eyes. He picked her up and hugged her. He said, "Bella, I'm so sorry. I love you. You're my best friend. Please don't go."

But Bella could not hear him. She closed her eyes and went to sleep. She never woke up again. She never got to play with the ball or eat the delicious treats or feel Sam's hugs. She was gone.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big green slide that looked very fun. They ran to the slide and took turns to go down. They laughed and shouted with joy.

But then, they saw a boy who was smaller than them. He also wanted to play on the slide, but he was shy and scared. Tim and Kim did not want to share the slide with him. They said, "This is our slide. You cannot play here. Go away!"

The boy felt sad and angry. He said, "You are mean and selfish. You do not know how to share. I will show you!" He ran away and came back with a big skeleton. He said, "This is my friend. He is very strong and scary. He will make you go away!"

Tim and Kim were frightened by the skeleton. They screamed and ran away from the slide. They hid behind a tree and cried. They wished they had been nice to the boy and shared the slide with him.

The boy smiled and said, "This is not a real skeleton. It is a toy. I made it with some sticks and some paper. I wanted to teach you a lesson. You should not be mean and selfish. You should be kind and generous. Sharing is caring!"

Tim and Kim realized they had been wrong. They felt sorry and ashamed. They came out from behind the tree and said, "We are sorry. You are right. We should not be mean and selfish. We should be kind and generous. Sharing is caring. Can we be your friends?"

The boy nodded and said, "Yes, you can be my friends. Let us play on the slide together. It is more fun when we share." They all went to the slide and took turns to go down. They laughed and shouted with joy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Be kind and generous to others. Do not be mean and selfish. You will make more friends and have more fun.

The next day, Timmy woke up and saw that the sun was shining. He was glad because he could go outside to play again. But when he got to the forest, he saw that someone had cut down all the trees. Timmy was very upset because he loved the trees and the animals that lived in them. He went home and told his mom what had happened.

His mom called the police and they found out that a man had cut down the trees without a permit. The man was punished for what he did and the trees were able to grow back. Timmy was glad that the trees were safe and he could play in the wild forest again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy monster named Frank. Frank was very mean and liked to destroy things. One day, Frank was walking through the forest when he saw a tiny inchworm crawling on a leaf. Frank thought it would be funny to step on the inchworm and destroy it.

But just as Frank was about to stomp on the inchworm, he heard a tiny voice say, "Please don't hurt me!" It was the inchworm talking! Frank was surprised to hear the little creature speak. He looked down and saw the inchworm's tiny, inch-long body.

Frank felt bad for wanting to destroy the inchworm. Instead, he decided to let the little creature go and promised to never hurt anything again. From that day on, Frank became a kind monster and made friends with all the animals in the forest, including the inchworm.

When the cookies were finally done, Lily's mommy gave one to her little brother. But he was still upset and threw the cookie on the floor. The cookie broke into many thin pieces. Lily's mommy got even more upset and sent her little brother to his room.

"Who are you?" Lila asked, feeling surprised.

"I am a squirrel, a squirrel, a squirrel," the voice said. "I live in this tree, this tree, this tree. Do you want to come and play, play, play?"

Lila and Tom looked at each other. They felt scared and excited. They did not know what to do. Should they go into the hole and meet the squirrel? Or should they run away and stay in the field?

"That is how horses say hello. They neigh. They also snort, whinny and nicker. They have different sounds for different feelings."

"Oh, I see," Tom said. "Can we try to talk to the horse?"

"Sure, you can try," mom said. "But be gentle and respectful. Horses are very smart and sensitive animals."

Tom and Mia nodded and moved closer to the fence again. They tried to imitate the horse's sounds. They neighed, snorted, whinnied and nickered. The horse seemed to like their attempts. It moved its ears and nose and made some sounds back.

They were having fun until the horse did something unexpected. It lifted its tail and farted. A loud and smelly fart. Tom and Mia covered their noses and giggled. The horse looked embarrassed. It lowered its head and walked away.

"Oops, I think we made the horse shy," Mia said.

"Maybe it was just an accident," Tom said.

"Or maybe it was trying to tell us something," mom said.

"Like what?" Tom and Mia asked.

"Like, maybe it was time to say goodbye and thank you for the visit," mom said.

Tom and Mia agreed. They waved to the horse and said, "Bye, horse! Thank you for talking to us. You are very funny. We hope to see you again soon."

The horse looked back and nodded. It made a soft nicker. It seemed to say, "You are welcome. You are very kind. Come back anytime."

But as she slept, the bubble popped! Lily woke up to find herself covered in sticky goo. She cried and cried, but the bubble was gone forever. From that day on, Lily learned that sometimes the things we love can hurt us.

As they got on the plane, Timmy's mom warned him not to spoil his dinner with too many snacks. Timmy promised he wouldn't. But as the plane took off, Timmy saw the snacks and couldn't resist. He ate and ate until he felt sick. He remembered his promise to his mom and felt bad.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who loved to eat fruit. He lived in a big tree with lots of fruit. One day, a bird came and asked the monkey if he could have some fruit. The monkey said yes and gave the bird a big juicy apple. 

The bird was very happy and thanked the monkey. But then, a sneaky squirrel came and stole some fruit from the monkey's tree. The monkey saw the squirrel and got very angry. He said to the squirrel, "You shouldn't steal from others. It's not nice."

The squirrel felt bad and apologized to the monkey. From that day on, the squirrel was more modest and only took the fruit that fell on the ground. The monkey forgave the squirrel and they became friends. The moral of the story is that it's important to be honest and not take things that don't belong to you.

The mouse said, "I'm sorry. I'll close the door now." 

The bird said, "Thank you. I like my structure to be closed when I'm inside."

Poppy was a red flower who lived in a big garden. She liked to dance in the sun and talk to the bees. She was happy and friendly to everyone.

But there was one thing that Poppy hated. She hated spicy food. She thought it was too hot and made her mouth hurt. She only liked sweet and soft food, like honey and bread.

One day, a new family moved into the house next to the garden. They liked to cook spicy food every day. They used a lot of pepper and garlic and onion. The smell of the spicy food came into the garden and made Poppy feel sick.

Poppy tried to hide from the smell. She moved to the other side of the garden, behind a big tree. But the wind blew the smell everywhere. She covered her nose with her petals, but she could still smell it. She wished the new family would stop cooking spicy food.

Then, one day, something wonderful happened. A little girl came out of the house and walked into the garden. She saw Poppy and smiled. She picked her gently and brought her to her room. She put her in a vase with water and said, "You are so pretty, Poppy. I love you."

Poppy felt happy and loved. She did not smell the spicy food anymore. She smelled the girl's perfume and soap. She liked the girl very much. She decided that maybe the new family was not so bad after all. She hoped the girl would come back and visit her every day.

"Help, help!" Ben shouted. "We need water!"

Anna grabbed a bucket and filled it with water from the hose. She threw the water on the fire and the smoke. The fire and the smoke went away.

"Phew, that was close!" Anna said. "Are you okay, Ben?"

Ben nodded, but he looked sad. He took off the necklace and gave it back to Anna.

"Here, you can have the treasure," he said. "I'm sorry I burned our cookies. They were yummy."

Anna hugged him and smiled.

"It's okay, Ben," she said. "The cookies were just a snack. You are my real treasure. And we still have our map and our flashlight. We can still be explorers."

Ben hugged her back and smiled too.

"Thanks, Anna," he said. "You are my real treasure too. And we still have our tent. We can still be in the jungle."

They cleaned up the mess and went back to their tent. They ate some fruit instead of cookies and looked at their map. They planned their next adventure. They were happy.

Lily nodded. She liked to play hide and seek. She closed her eyes and counted. "One, two, three..."

Sam lifted the lid and climbed into the bin. It was dark and smelly. He heard Lily counting. He hoped she would not find him soon.

"Nine, ten. Ready or not, here I come!" Lily opened her eyes and looked around. She saw the slide, the swing and the bin. She ran to the bin and lifted the lid.

"Found you!" she shouted. She saw Sam's face in the bin. He looked scared and dirty. She laughed.

Sam felt embarrassed. He wanted to hide in the bin, not be found in the bin. He tried to get out, but he slipped and fell back in. He heard more laughter. He looked up and saw other children pointing and giggling at him.

"Look at Sam, he is in the bin! He is so silly and smelly!" they said.

Lily felt sorry for Sam. She did not want to laugh at him. She wanted to help him. She reached out her hand and pulled him out of the bin.

"Are you okay, Sam?" she asked.

Sam nodded. He was okay, but he felt dull. He did not want to play hide and seek anymore. He wanted to go home and wash.

"Let's go, Lily. I don't like the bin. It is not fun. It is yucky."

Tim saw Kim and felt sorry for her. He also felt thirsty, but he did not care about the pebble anymore. He saw the frog that had jumped off his head and was now sitting on a rock. He thought the frog was funny and cute. He went to the pond and drank some water. He also said hello to the frog.

"Hello, frog. You are green and wet. Do you like the pond?" he asked.

The frog croaked and nodded. He liked the pond and the water and the lily pads. He did not like the pebble, because it was hard and dry and dull.

Tim smiled and said, "You are right, frog. The pebble is not important. It is just a rock. The pond is better. It has water and fish and frogs. And it has you, my new friend."

He looked at Kim and said, "Kim, do you want to play with me and the frog? We can share the pebble, if you want. Or we can leave it here, and find something else to play with. There are many things in the yard that are fun and nice."

Kim heard Tim and looked at him. She also looked at the frog and the pond. She felt silly and sad. She had been greedy and mean. She had not been a good sister or a good friend. She did not want the pebble anymore. She wanted to play with Tim and the frog. She wanted to drink some water and cool off. She wanted to say sorry and be happy.

She let go of the pebble and threw it back into the pond. She ran to Tim and hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Tim. You are right. The pebble is not important. You are important. You are my brother and my friend. I want to play with you and the frog. Can we share the pond and the water and the lily pads?"

Tim hugged her back and said, "Of course, Kim. I'm sorry, too. You are important. You are my sister and my friend. We can share everything in the yard, because we have each other. And we have the frog, too. He is our friend, too."

The frog croaked and smiled. He was happy that Tim and Kim had made up. He jumped into the water and swam to them. He invited them to join him and play in the pond. They agreed and followed him. They splashed and laughed and had fun. They forgot about the pebble, because they had something better. They had water and fish and frogs. And they had love and friendship. They were wealthy, because they had each other.

They were angry and sad that Sara and Ben were playing with their bones. They wanted to rest in peace. They started to move and make noises. They wanted to scare Sara and Ben away.

Sara and Ben heard the noises and saw the skeletons move. They were terrified. They dropped the bones and ran out of the room. They slammed the door and ran out of the old house. They never went back there again.

Sara and Ben learned a lesson. They learned that some things are not for playing. They learned that some things are delicate and need respect. They learned that some things are better left alone.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and books. But today they have a quarrel. Lily wants to play with the red car. Tom wants to play with the red car too.

"It is my car!" Lily says. "I saw it first!"

"No, it is my car!" Tom says. "I like it more!"

They pull the car from each other. They are angry and sad.

Mom sees them. She is not happy. She says, "Stop, Lily and Tom! You are not nice to each other. You have to share the toys. Why don't you play with the light?"

Lily and Tom look at the light. It is a flashlight. It can make bright and dark. It can make shapes and colors. It is fun.

"Can we play with the light, Mom?" Lily asks.

"Yes, you can," Mom says. "But you have to take turns. And you have to say sorry to each other."

Lily and Tom say sorry. They hug. They are friends again. They play with the light. They make a star, a moon, a heart, and a smile. They laugh and have fun. They forget the quarrel. They are happy.

Anna and Ben love to visit their grandma and grandpa on the farm. They like to see the animals and help with the chores. The farm is very noisy, but they do not mind.

One day, they went to feed the chickens with grandpa. They carried a bucket of corn and threw some on the ground. The chickens clucked and pecked and ran after the corn. Anna and Ben laughed and tried to pet them.

"Be careful, they might peck you," grandpa said.

"Why do they peck, grandpa?" Anna asked.

"They peck to eat and to protect themselves. They are not very friendly, but they give us eggs," grandpa explained.

"Can we see the eggs, grandpa?" Ben asked.

"Sure, let's go to the coop and collect them," grandpa said.

They walked to the coop and saw many eggs in the nests. Grandpa gave Anna and Ben a basket and told them to pick up the eggs gently. They filled the basket with white and brown eggs.

"Wow, so many eggs!" Anna said.

"Can we eat them, grandpa?" Ben said.

"Of course, we can make a yummy breakfast with them. Grandma will be happy," grandpa said.

They carried the basket back to the house, where grandma was waiting for them. She hugged them and praised them for their work.

"You are such good helpers, Anna and Ben. I love you very much," grandma said.

"We love you too, grandma. And we love the farm," Anna and Ben said.

One day, a small boy named Tom wanted to make cocoa for his mom. He saw a big pot on the stove and a box of cocoa on the shelf. He climbed on a chair and reached for the box. He opened it and poured some cocoa into the pot. Then he turned on the stove and waited.

But he did not know how to make cocoa. He put too much cocoa and not enough water. The pot started to boil and bubble. The cocoa spilled over and made a big mess. Tom was scared and did not know what to do.

He heard his mom coming and quickly turned off the stove. He ran to the door and said, "Mom, I made cocoa for you, but it went reverse!"

His mom saw the cocoa all over the stove and the floor. She was not happy, but she was not angry either. She hugged Tom and said, "Thank you for trying to make cocoa for me, but reverse means to go back, not to go wrong. Next time, let me help you, okay?"

Tom nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry for the mess. Can we still have cocoa?"

His mom smiled and said, "Of course we can. But first, let's clean up this mess together. Then we can make some new cocoa and drink it together. How does that sound?"

Tom smiled and said, "That sounds good, mom. I love you."

His mom said, "I love you too, Tom." And they cleaned up the mess and made some new cocoa and drank it together.

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play outside. They had a scooter that they shared, but sometimes they fought over it. One day, they saw a new scooter in the store window. It was shiny and red, and had a horn and a basket. They both wanted it very much.

"Can we have it, Mom?" they asked, pulling her hand.

Mom looked at the price tag and shook her head. "No, it's too much money. We have a scooter at home, remember?"

"But it's old and boring," Ben said. "And it has a scratch and a wobble."

"And it's too small for both of us," Mia said. "We need a new scooter, Mom. Please!"

Mom sighed. She knew they loved the scooter, but they also had to learn to be happy with what they had. She decided to teach them a lesson.

"Okay, fine. You can have the new scooter, but only if you give me the old one. I'll store it in the garage, and you can never use it again. Deal?"

Ben and Mia looked at each other. They thought Mom was being harsh, but they really wanted the new scooter. They nodded and said, "Deal."

Mom paid for the new scooter and gave it to them. They were so excited that they ran outside and took turns riding it. They honked the horn and put their toys in the basket. They felt very lucky and happy.

But after a while, they started to miss the old scooter. They remembered how they had fun with it, how they decorated it with stickers and ribbons, how they raced and chased each other with it. They realized that the old scooter was not so bad after all. They felt sorry for giving it away.

They ran back to the store and asked Mom if they could have the old scooter back. Mom smiled and said, "Sure, you can have it back. But only if you give me the new one. I'll store it in the garage, and you can never use it again. Deal?"

Ben and Mia looked at each other. They knew Mom was being smart, but they also learned their lesson. They nodded and said, "Deal."

Mom gave them the old scooter and took the new one. They hugged her and thanked her. They rode the old scooter home, feeling very happy and grateful. They decided to share it and take good care of it. They realized that the best scooter was the one they had.

Lily loved her bear very much. She gave him a name: Bobo. She took him everywhere: to the park, to the store, to the bed. She liked to talk to him and pretend he talked back. She told him stories and secrets and jokes.

One day, Lily and her mom went to visit grandma. Grandma had a big house with many rooms and things. Lily wanted to show Bobo to grandma and make her happy. She ran to the living room with Bobo in her arms. But when she got there, she saw something that made her stop.

On the couch, there was another bear. He was bigger and older and darker than Bobo. He had a red ribbon around his neck and a tag that said: "This is Bruno. He belongs to grandma. He is very special and old. Please be gentle with him."

Lily felt a pang in her heart. She looked at Bobo and then at Bruno. She wondered if grandma liked Bruno more than Bobo. She wondered if Bruno was a better bear than Bobo. She wondered if she should leave Bobo on the couch and play with Bruno instead.

She walked slowly to the couch and put Bobo next to Bruno. She touched Bruno's fur and his ribbon. He felt soft and smooth. She picked him up and hugged him. He felt heavy and warm. She said: "Hello, Bruno. I'm Lily. You are a nice bear."

Then she heard a voice behind her. It was grandma. She smiled and said: "Hello, Lily. I'm so happy to see you. And I see you met Bruno. He is my oldest and dearest friend. I got him when I was a little girl, just like you. He has been with me through many things. He is very precious to me."

Lily turned around and saw grandma's eyes. They were bright and kind. She saw grandma's hands. They were wrinkled and gentle. She saw grandma's face. It was proud and loving. She felt a warmth in her chest. She said: "Grandma, I want to show you something. This is Bobo. He is my best friend. I got him for my birthday. He has been with me everywhere. He is very special to me."

Grandma nodded and said: "I can see that, Lily. He is a beautiful bear. He looks very happy and well-loved. He reminds me of Bruno when he was young. I'm sure they will get along very well. Why don't you bring them both to the kitchen and we can have some cookies and milk and talk some more?"

Lily smiled and said: "Okay, grandma. That sounds good." She took Bobo and Bruno in her arms and followed grandma to the kitchen. She felt proud and happy. She had two bears and one grandma. She had a lot of love.

"Let's pretend we are flying on the carpet," Lily said. "We can go to the places on the map and have adventures."

Tom and Lily felt sorry. They did not mean to upset their grandma. They got off the carpet and tried to fold it neatly.

"Grandma, we are sorry," Lily said. "We were just pretending. We did not know the carpet was so special."

The boy does not answer.

"Do you want to play with us?" Ben asks.

The boy shakes his head.

"Why not?" Lila asks.

The boy points to his ears. He makes a sign with his fingers.

"He can't hear us," Ben says. "He is deaf."

"Yes, maybe we can," Ben says.

"What does that mean?" Lila asks.

Ben thinks hard. He remembers seeing a book about sign language in the library.

Lila and Ben make the same sign with their fingers. They feel happy. They have a new friend. They wonder what else they can learn from him.

Tom and Mia were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with many round and soft fruits. They were peaches. Tom and Mia wanted to try them, but they did not know if they could.

"Who owns these peaches?" Tom asked.

"I don't know. Maybe the tree owns them," Mia said.

"But the tree does not eat them. Maybe we can have some," Tom said.

He reached for a peach, but a loud voice stopped him.

"Hey, what are you doing? Those are my peaches!" The voice belonged to a man who was sitting under the tree. He looked angry.

Tom and Mia were scared and confused. They did not know the man or why he owned the peaches.

"Sorry, sir. We did not know. We just wanted to taste them," Mia said.

"Well, you can't. These are my peaches. I planted this tree and I take care of it. You have to ask me before you touch them," the man said.

He picked a peach and gave it to Tom and Mia.

"Here, you can have one each. But don't come back without my permission. And don't forget to say thank you," he said.

Tom and Mia took the peaches and said thank you. They ran away from the tree and the man. They ate the peaches and they were sweet and juicy. But they still felt confused.

"Why does he own the peaches? Why can't we share them?" Tom asked.

"I don't know. Maybe he likes them too much. Or maybe he is lonely and needs them," Mia said.

They decided to play with their ball instead. They did not want to make the man angry again. They hoped he would be happy with his peaches.

Sam and Ben were brothers who liked to play in the yard. One day, they found a big nest with four eggs in it. They wanted to see what was inside the eggs, so they took them to their room.

"Let's break them open and look," Sam said.

"No, that's bad. We should quit and put them back," Ben said. He was more intelligent than Sam and knew that the eggs had baby birds in them.

But Sam did not listen. He broke one egg with a hammer and saw a wet and bloody thing inside. He felt sick and scared.

"See, I told you. Quit, Sam, quit!" Ben shouted.

But Sam did not quit. He broke another egg and another. He wanted to see if they were all the same. He did not care about the baby birds.

Then, they heard a loud squawk from the window. It was the mother bird. She saw what Sam had done to her eggs and was very angry. She flew into the room and attacked Sam with her beak and claws. She scratched his face and eyes and made him bleed.

"Help, help!" Sam cried.

But Ben did not help. He was too mad at Sam for being bad and stupid. He ran out of the room and left Sam alone with the angry bird.

The end.

"Let's go to the kitchen," Ben whispered to Lily. "Maybe we can find some cheese."

Lily nodded. She loved cheese. They got out of their beds and tiptoed to the door. They opened it slowly and looked around. The coast was clear.

"Help me, Lily," he said. "Push me."

Lily pushed Ben, but he lost his balance. He fell off the chair and pulled the cheese with him. The cheese landed on his head and made a loud thud.

"Ow!" Ben cried. "That hurt!"

Lily jumped off the chair and ran to Ben. She saw the cheese on his head and laughed.

"Look, Ben, you have a cheese hat!" she said.

Ben was not amused. He took the cheese off his head and threw it on the floor. He was angry and sad.

"That's not funny, Lily," he said. "You made me fall. And now the cheese is dirty. We can't eat it."

"Maybe we can tie it back together," Lily said.

Ben shook his head. He said, "That won't work, Lily. Cheese is not like a shoe. You can't tie it."

They heard footsteps. They looked up and saw their mom. She saw the cheese on the floor and the chair on the side. She knew what happened.

She was not happy. She said, "Lily and Ben, what did you do? You were supposed to nap. And you made a mess with the cheese. That was not nice."

Lily and Ben followed their mom. They were not restless anymore. They were tired and sorry. They learned their lesson. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We love you. And we love cheese. But not on our heads."

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked. "The bee is not mean. It is just scared. It thinks you are a big cat. You have to be careful with bees. They are unique. They have a special job in the garden. They help the flowers grow and make sweet honey. But they also have a sting to protect themselves. You have to respect them and not bother them."

Lily nodded. She understood. She was sorry for the bee. She hoped it was okay too.

"Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. And a good dog," Lily said.

They smiled and went inside. They put some ice on Lily's nose and ate some honey. They learned something new about bees. And they decided to act like other animals next time.

"Help! Rex wants Ducky!" Lily cried.

"Mom! Rex took Ducky!" they shouted.

She returned to the pool and gave Ducky and the chocolates to Tom and Lily. They were happy and thanked her. They also thanked the neighbor and said they were sorry for Rex. They said they would share Ducky with him sometimes, if he was nice.

They learned a lesson that day: to be compassionate to others, even if they make mistakes. They also learned to appreciate their treats and their toys. They enjoyed swimming with Ducky and eating chocolates, and they made a new friend: Rex.

Lily was a poor girl who lived in a hut with her mother. They had no money and no food. Lily was always hungry and sad. She liked to go to the forest and look for mushrooms. Mushrooms were her favorite food. She hoped to find some big and juicy ones.

One day, she saw a big mushroom under a tree. It was red and white and smelled good. Lily ran to pick it, but a voice stopped her.

"Wait, little girl. Don't touch that mushroom. It is not good for you. It is a magic mushroom. It can make you dream strange things."

Lily looked around and saw a fairy sitting on a branch. She had wings and a wand and a dress made of flowers. Lily was surprised and scared.

"Who are you?" she asked.

"I am a fairy. I live in this forest. I watch over the animals and the plants. And I watch over you, too. I know you are poor and hungry. But you must not eat that mushroom. It will not fill your belly. It will only fill your head with dreams. Dreams that are not real. Dreams that can make you forget what is important."

Lily was curious and tempted. She wanted to see what dreams the mushroom could give her. Maybe she could dream of a big house and a lot of food and a happy family. Maybe she could dream of being a princess or a fairy or a hero. She reached for the mushroom again.

"Please, fairy. Let me try it. Just once. I want to see something different. I want to be happy."

The fairy shook her head.

"No, Lily. Trust me. Dreams are not enough. You need to work hard and be brave and be kind. You need to help your mother and yourself. You need to find real food and real friends and real happiness. That is the only way to make your life better. The mushroom will only make you lose your way."

Lily looked at the fairy and then at the mushroom. She thought for a moment. She realized the fairy was right. She did not want to live in a dream. She wanted to live in the real world. She wanted to make it a better place. She let go of the mushroom and smiled at the fairy.

"Thank you, fairy. You are very wise and very good. I will listen to you. I will not eat the mushroom. I will go home and help my mother. I will look for real mushrooms and real happiness. And maybe, someday, I will see you again."

The fairy smiled back and nodded.

"You are welcome, Lily. You are very smart and very brave. I am proud of you. I will always watch over you. And maybe, someday, we will meet again. Goodbye, Lily. And remember: dreams are good, but only when they inspire you to do good."

Lily waved goodbye and ran back to her hut. She felt happy and hopeful. She had learned a valuable lesson. She had made a new friend. And she had found a new dream. A dream of being a good person.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray mouse named Boomer. Boomer was very brave and kind. He loved to explore the world and have new adventures. 

One day, Boomer was out walking by a pond and spotted a fish. Boomer was so excited! He wanted to get a closer look, so he started to walk towards it. 

Suddenly, Boomer felt something pinch his back! He was scared and spun around, but he couldn't see anything. Suddenly, Boomer heard a voice. It said, "Don't come any closer, little mouse! I am protecting this fish."

Boomer saw a big frog. He said, "It's okay, I'm not here to hurt it. I just want to take a look." 

The frog tapped its webbed foot on the ground and said, "No. This fish needs my protection. I can't let you get too close."

One day, a sailor went to the sea. He had a big boat. He wanted to try to catch some fish. The sky was blue and the sun was bright. The sailor was very happy.

But then, the wind started to blow. The waves got big and the boat rocked. The sailor got scared. He said, "Oh no! This is bad. I need to go back to land."

The sailor tried very hard to sail back. He pulled on the ropes and turned the boat around. The wind blew and the waves splashed, but he did not give up. 

Finally, the sailor got back to land. He was wet and tired, but he was safe. He said, "I am happy to be back on land. Next time, I will be more careful when I go to the sea." And from that day, the sailor always checked the weather before he went to catch fish.

"Hi Bunny!" said Henny. "I have a big egg for you. I hope you like it!"

"Thank you, Henny!" said Bunny. "You are very kind!"

But when Henny went to get the egg, it was gone! It had vanished! Henny and Bunny looked everywhere. They searched high and low, but they could not find the egg.

As they were searching, they met their friend, Squirrel. Squirrel had seen the egg and knew where it was. "Friends, I saw your egg!" said Squirrel. "It rolled down the hill and into a big bush."

Henny, Bunny, and Squirrel went to the bush and found the egg. Henny was so happy! She gave the egg to Bunny, and they all played together. From that day on, they were the best of friends, and Henny continued to share her eggs with everyone in the village.

Suddenly, Tim lost his balance and the bag fell down. All the hard rocks came out of the bag. His friends saw what happened and ran to help him. They all laughed and helped Tim pick up the rocks. Tim learned that it's more fun to play with friends than to try to impress them.

One day, a big dog and a little cat were playing near a hedge. They liked to throw a small ball to each other. The sun was bright, and the grass was soft.

After some time, the dog got tired. He wanted to stop playing, but the cat wanted to keep throwing the ball. The dog said, "I am tired. I want to rest." The cat did not listen and threw the ball again.

The dog was sad and sat down by the hedge. The cat saw the dog was tired and stopped throwing the ball. They both lay down in the shade of the hedge and took a nap together. The dog and the cat were happy, and they stayed good friends.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a lively train with a big engine. The train loved to go fast and make all the kids happy. The kids would wave and cheer as the train went by.

One day, the train met a wise old owl. The owl said, "I recommend you go to the big hill and make a fun ride for the kids." The train thought that was a great idea and went to the big hill.

The lively train went up and down the big hill, making the kids very happy. They laughed and clapped as the train's engine went fast. The train and the kids had a fun day, all thanks to the wise old owl's recommendation.

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his wheel. He would push it with his nose and run after it. The wheel was easy for Spot to play with because it was not too heavy. Spot was a very happy dog.

One day, Spot was playing with his wheel when a small cat named Fluffy came by. Fluffy wanted to play with the wheel too, but it was too heavy for her. Spot did not want to share his wheel, so they started to fight. Fluffy was sad because she could not play with the wheel.

Then, Spot had an idea. He found a small stick and put it in the middle of the wheel. Now, Fluffy could push the stick and the wheel would move. The stick made it easy for Fluffy to play with the wheel. They both played with the wheel together and became best friends.

Sara was a gifted girl. She could draw, sing and dance very well. She liked to keep her work in a big book. She showed her work to her mom and dad every day. They were very proud of her.

One day, Sara went to the park with her mom. She saw a boy playing with a ball. He kicked the ball very hard and it flew over the fence. The boy was sad. He could not get his ball back.

Sara wanted to help the boy. She had an idea. She took out her big book and a crayon. She drew a picture of the boy and his ball. She gave the picture to the boy and said, "Here, this is for you. You can keep it. It is my work. I hope you like it."

The boy smiled. He looked at the picture. He saw his face and his ball. He liked it very much. He said, "Thank you, Sara. You are very gifted. You are very kind. Can I be your friend?"

Sara nodded. She was happy. She said, "Yes, you can be my friend. Do you want to play with me?"

The boy nodded. He said, "Yes, I want to play with you. What do you want to play?"

Sara said, "Let's play draw, sing and dance. I can teach you. It is fun."

The boy said, "OK, let's play. You can teach me. It sounds fun."

Sara and the boy played together. They drew, sang and danced. They had a lot of fun. They became good friends. Sara's mom watched them and smiled. She was glad that Sara shared her work and made a new friend.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play and have fun. They also liked to eat dessert, like cake and ice cream. But sometimes they had to stay in their room and wait for dinner. They did not like that.

One day, they heard Mom and Dad talking in the kitchen. They sounded happy and excited. Lily and Ben were nosy. They wanted to know what was going on. They sneaked out of their room and tiptoed to the kitchen door. They peeked inside.

They saw a big chocolate cake on the table, with candles and sprinkles. They also saw a present wrapped in shiny paper. It was for them! Mom and Dad were planning a surprise party for their birthday!

Lily and Ben were so happy. They wanted to eat the cake and open the present. But they also wanted to keep the surprise. They decided to go back to their room and pretend they did not see anything. They waited for Mom and Dad to call them.

Soon, they heard Mom and Dad singing "Happy Birthday" and knocking on their door. They opened it and acted surprised. Mom and Dad hugged them and said they were proud of them. They brought them to the kitchen and gave them the cake and the present. Lily and Ben thanked them and smiled. They ate the cake and ice cream and opened the present. It was a big box of toys and books. They were so happy. They had the best birthday ever. And they learned that sometimes it was good to stay in their room.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play with their toys in the garden. Tom has a red car and Sue has a blue bike. They race each other and have fun.

One day, Tom's car breaks. The wheel falls off and the car does not move. Tom is sad. He does not want to play anymore.

Sue sees Tom's car. She says, "I can help you. I can repair your car. I have a green box with tools. We can fix the wheel with a screw and a hammer."

Tom smiles. He says, "Thank you, Sue. You are a good friend. Can I see your green box?"

Sue nods. She runs to her house and brings her green box. She opens it and shows Tom her tools. They are shiny and new.

They work together to repair Tom's car. They find a screw that fits the wheel and a hammer to hit it. They are careful and gentle. They do not hurt themselves or the car.

Soon, Tom's car is fixed. The wheel is on and the car can move. Tom and Sue are happy. They hug each other and say, "We did it!"

They go back to the garden and play with their toys. They race each other and have fun. They see a fat cat on the fence. The cat is lazy and sleepy. It does not care about their toys. It only wants to nap.

Tom and Sue laugh. They say, "Look at the fat cat. It is funny and cute. We like the fat cat."

They play until it is dark. Then they say goodbye and go to their houses. They are tired and hungry. They have dinner and go to bed. They dream of their toys and their green box and their fat cat. They are happy.

One day, Sam and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw a big dog with a long tail and a shiny collar. The dog was friendly and licked their faces. They asked their mom if they could pet the dog.

"Sure, but be gentle and ask the owner first," their mom said.

They looked around and saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a book and a cup of coffee. He also had a rope in his hand. The rope was attached to the dog's collar. The man was the dog's owner.

"Excuse me, sir, can we pet your dog?" Sam asked.

"Of course, his name is Max. He loves children," the man said. He smiled and put down his book.

Sam and Lily ran to Max and hugged him. They felt his soft fur and his warm breath. They scratched his ears and his belly. Max wagged his tail and barked happily.

"Wow, he's so big and nice. Can we play with him?" Lily asked.

"Sure, but you have to hold his rope. He likes to run and chase things," the man said. He gave them the rope and told them to be careful.

Sam and Lily took turns holding the rope. They led Max around the park. They threw a ball and he fetched it. They ran and he followed them. They had a lot of fun with Max.

But then, something bad happened. Lily tripped over a rock and fell down. She let go of the rope. Max saw a squirrel and ran after it. He was very fast and soon he was out of sight.

"Max, come back!" Sam and Lily shouted.

They got up and ran after him. They were scared and worried. They did not want to lose Max. They did not want to make the man sad.

They looked everywhere, but they could not find Max. They felt like crying. They did not know what to do.

Then, they heard a familiar bark. They turned around and saw Max. He was coming back to them. He had the squirrel in his mouth. He dropped it and licked their faces.

"Max, you're back! We're so happy!" Sam and Lily said.

They hugged him and took his rope. They were relieved and glad. They did not care that their pants were dirty and torn. They did not care that the squirrel was angry and ran away. They only cared that Max was safe and sound.

They went back to the man and apologized. They told him what happened. They said they were sorry for letting go of the rope.

The man was not angry. He was understanding and kind. He said it was okay. He said Max was a good dog, but sometimes he was too curious and playful. He said they were brave and responsible for bringing him back.

He thanked them and gave them a treat. He said they could pet Max anytime they wanted. He said they were his new friends.

Sam and Lily thanked him and said goodbye. They said they loved Max and they would visit him again. They said he was not an ordinary dog. He was a special dog.

They went home with their mom. They told her everything. She was proud of them and hugged them. She said they had a big adventure. She said they learned a lot.

They agreed and smiled. They said they had a great day. They said they made a new friend. They said they liked to lead Max. They said they did not mind their pants. They said they were happy.

Sam is a dog. He likes to run and play with his owner, Ben. Ben is a boy. He likes to throw a ball and Sam likes to catch it. They are good friends.

One day, Sam and Ben go to the park. They see many things. They see trees and flowers and birds and squirrels. Sam wants to chase the squirrels, but Ben says no. He says they are wild and they might bite. Sam listens to Ben. He is a good dog.

But then, Sam sees something else. He sees a shiny thing on the ground. It is a coin. Sam is curious. He wants to examine it. He runs to the coin and sniffs it. It smells like metal. He licks it. It tastes like metal. He picks it up with his mouth. It feels like metal.

"Sam, what are you doing?" Ben asks. He sees Sam with the coin. He runs to him. He wants the coin. He says it is his. He says he can buy candy with it. He reaches for the coin.

But Sam does not want to give the coin. He likes the coin. He thinks it is his. He growls at Ben. He shows his teeth. He is a wild dog.

"Sam, no!" Ben says. He is scared. He does not like Sam's growl. He does not like Sam's teeth. He does not understand why Sam is angry. He loves Sam. He says he is sorry. He says he will share the candy. He tries to calm Sam down.

Sam hears Ben's voice. He sees Ben's face. He remembers Ben is his owner. He remembers Ben is his friend. He feels sorry. He drops the coin. He licks Ben's hand. He is a good dog again.

Ben hugs Sam. He says he is happy. He says he forgives Sam. He says he loves Sam. He picks up the coin. He says they will buy candy together. He says they will share it. He says they are good friends.

Sam wags his tail. He says he is happy too. He says he loves Ben. He says he is sorry for being wild. He says he will not do it again. He says he is a good dog.

They walk to the candy store. They are happy. They are friends. They are owner and dog.

Tom likes to play in the garden. He likes to look at the flowers and the trees and the birds. He also likes to find bugs. He thinks bugs are nice and fun. He has a jar where he keeps some bugs. He gives them grass and water and talks to them.

One day, he finds a big bug in the grass. It has many legs and a hard shell. It is brown and shiny. Tom thinks it is a nice bug. He picks it up and puts it in his jar. He says, "Hello, bug. You are my new friend. Do you like your new home?"

The bug does not say anything. It moves its legs and tries to get out of the jar. Tom does not see that. He is happy with his bug. He takes the jar to his mom. He says, "Mom, look at my bug. It is a nice bug. Can I keep it?"

Mom looks at the jar. She sees the bug. She does not think it is a nice bug. She thinks it is a bad bug. She knows it can bite and hurt Tom. She says, "Tom, that is not a nice bug. That is a mean bug. It is called a scorpion. You have to let it go. It can hurt you and your other bugs."

Tom is sad. He does not want to let go of his bug. He says, "But mom, it is a nice bug. It does not bite me. It is my friend."

Mom says, "No, Tom, it is not your friend. It is a wild bug. It belongs in the garden, not in a jar. Trust me, Tom, it is better for you and the bug to let it go."

Tom listens to his mom. He knows she loves him and wants him to be safe. He takes the jar back to the garden. He opens the lid and lets the bug go. The bug runs away and hides under a rock. Tom says, "Goodbye, bug. I hope you are happy in the garden. Maybe I will see you again."

Tom feels a little sad, but he also feels good. He knows he did the right thing. He looks around and sees many other bugs. He thinks they are nice and fun. He says, "Hello, bugs. Do you want to be my friends?"

Lily ran to her mom and said, "Mom, mom, I want to be in the show. Please, please, let me sign up."

Her mom looked at the poster and said, "Lily, you are too little for the show. The show is for big kids. You are only three. You can watch the show, but you cannot be in it."

Her mom said, "Lily, stop. You are being rude. You have to listen to me. I know what is best for you. You cannot be in the show. That is final."

Lily did not listen. She ran away from her mom and went to the school. She saw a table with a sign that said "Sign up here". She took a pen and wrote her name on a paper. She smiled and said, "I did it. I am in the show."

The next day, Lily went to the school with her mom. She saw the stage with lights and curtains and chairs. She saw the big kids in costumes and makeup. She said, "Mom, look, there is the stage. I am going to be on it. I am going to sing and dance."

Her mom said, "Lily, what did you do? You signed up for the show? You did not listen to me. You are in trouble. You cannot be on the stage. You have to come with me."

Lily said, "No, no, I want to be on the stage. I want to be in the show. I insist, I insist, I insist."

Lily said, "I am sorry. I am sorry. I am sorry."

One day, a little mule was walking in the field with his mother. He saw a big gate that was closed. He wanted to see what was behind the gate.

"Mom, can I open the gate?" he asked.

"No, my son, you cannot open the gate. It is not safe. There are big dogs behind the gate. They will bark and bite you. You must stay with me in the field," his mother said.

But the little mule was curious and did not listen to his mother. He waited until she was busy eating grass and then he ran to the gate. He pushed it with his nose and it opened. He went inside.

"Wow, look at all the things here!" he said. He saw a big house, a car, a ball, and a bone. He wanted to play with them.

But then he heard a loud noise. It was the big dogs. They saw the little mule and they were angry. They ran to him and started to bark and bite him.

"Help, help!" the little mule cried. He was scared and hurt. He ran back to the gate, but it was closed. He did not know how to open it.

His mother heard his cry and came to the gate. She saw the big dogs and the little mule. She kicked the gate with her hooves and it opened. She ran to the little mule and chased away the big dogs. She hugged him and licked his wounds.

"I'm sorry, mom, I was wrong. I should have listened to you. You were right, it was not safe. I will never open the gate again," the little mule said.

"I'm glad you are safe, my son. I love you. But you must be careful and obey me. I know what is best for you. Come, let us go back to the field," his mother said.

They walked back to the field and the little mule learned his lesson. He never opened the gate again. He was happy with his mother and the grass.

"How can we invite it?" Lily asks. "It can't hear us. And it can't come to the sand. It is too dry for it."

Sam has an idea. He finds a big shell and a stick. He makes a hole in the shell. He puts the stick in the hole. He blows into the shell. It makes a loud sound.

"Maybe the shark can hear this," Sam says. He blows the shell again and again. He waves to the shark.

The shark hears the sound. It is curious. It swims closer to the sand. It sees Sam and Lily. They smile at it. They make signs with their hands. They want it to play with them.

The shark is happy. It wants to play with them too. It nods its head. It splashes the water with its tail. It makes bubbles with its mouth.

Lily and Sam laugh. They splash the water back. They make bubbles too. They have fun with the shark.

They are friends.

Sara liked to play with her shadow. She saw it on the wall when the sun was bright. She saw it on the floor when the lamp was on. She made her shadow do funny things. She made it jump, dance, and wave.

One day, Sara had a new idea. She wanted to talk to her shadow. She thought her shadow was intelligent. She said, "Hello, shadow. Do you want to be my friend?" She waited for an answer, but her shadow was silent. She said, "Please, shadow. Say something. I want to hear your voice."

Her shadow did not say anything. It only copied her movements. Sara felt sad. She thought her shadow did not like her. She said, "Why are you so quiet, shadow? Don't you like me? Don't you want to play with me?"

Her shadow still did not say anything. It only followed her steps. Sara felt angry. She said, "Fine, shadow. If you don't want to talk to me, I don't want to play with you. Go away, shadow. Leave me alone."

She turned off the lamp and ran to her bed. She covered herself with her blanket. She did not want to see her shadow anymore. She cried and cried.

But then, she heard a soft voice. It said, "Sara, Sara. Don't cry. I'm sorry, Sara. I can't talk to you. I'm only a shadow. But I like you, Sara. I want to play with you. Please, Sara. Don't be mad at me. Can we be friends again?"

Sara lifted her blanket and looked around. She saw her shadow on the wall. It was smiling and waving at her. Sara was surprised. She said, "Shadow, is that you? Are you talking to me?"

Her shadow said, "Yes, Sara. It's me. I'm talking to you. I learned how to talk from you. You are so intelligent, Sara. You taught me many words. Thank you, Sara. You are a good friend."

Sara smiled and wiped her tears. She said, "You're welcome, shadow. You are a good friend, too. I'm sorry I was mean to you. I didn't know you could talk. I'm happy you can talk. Can we play together?"

Her shadow said, "Of course, Sara. We can play together. We can have fun. We can be friends forever."

Sara turned on the lamp and got out of her bed. She hugged her shadow and said, "I love you, shadow. You are the best friend ever."

Her shadow hugged her back and said, "I love you, too, Sara. You are the best friend ever."

Lily was a little girl who loved to play with her doll. Her doll's name was Anna, and she had a pink dress and long hair. Lily took Anna everywhere, and they had many adventures together.

One day, Lily and Anna went to the park with Lily's mom. They saw a big slide, and Lily wanted to try it. She climbed up the ladder, holding Anna in her hand. She was very excited, and she slid down very fast. But when she reached the bottom, she let go of Anna by mistake. Anna flew out of her hand and landed on the ground.

Lily ran to pick up Anna, but she saw that Anna was hurt. Her dress was torn, and her hair was dirty. And worst of all, her face was cracked. Lily felt very sad, and she cried. She hugged Anna and said, "I'm sorry, Anna. I didn't mean to hurt you. You are my best friend."

Lily's mom saw what happened, and she came to comfort Lily. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can fix Anna. We can sew her dress, wash her hair, and glue her face. She will heal, and she will look as good as new. She is a very delicate doll, but she is also very strong. She loves you, and she knows you love her too."

Lily smiled, and she thanked her mom. She said, "Thank you, mom. You are very kind. Can we go home and fix Anna now?" Her mom nodded, and they went home. They worked together to heal Anna, and they gave her a new ribbon for her hair. Lily was very happy, and she said, "You are beautiful, Anna. You are my best friend." Anna smiled, and she said, "You are beautiful, Lily. You are my best friend." They hugged, and they played some more. They had many adventures together.

Lily was a little girl who liked to crawl. She crawled under the table, behind the sofa, and into the closet. She liked to pretend she was a cat, a snake, or a spy. She crawled very fast and very quiet.

One day, she crawled into the kitchen and saw a big cake on the counter. It was round and pink and had white cream on top. It looked very tasty. Lily wanted to have a bite, but she knew she had to wait for her mom to say yes.

She crawled closer to the cake and saw a little mouse on the floor. The mouse was nibbling on a crumb of cake. Lily was not afraid of the mouse. She liked animals. She crawled closer to the mouse and said hello.

The mouse was surprised to see Lily. He stopped nibbling and looked at her. He saw that she was friendly and not a cat. He gave her a wink and a smile. He offered her a crumb of cake.

Lily smiled back and took the crumb. She said thank you and ate it. It was very tasty. She winked at the mouse and gave him a hug. They became friends and shared the cake. They crawled away before mom came back. They had a lot of fun.

Lily loves to wash her toy vehicles. She has a red car, a blue truck, a yellow bus and a green tractor. She fills a bucket with water and soap and uses a sponge to make them shiny and clean.

One day, she sees a big vehicle parked outside her house. It is a fire engine. It has a ladder, a hose, a siren and a lot of lights. Lily thinks it is very cool and wants to wash it too.

She runs to the fire engine with her bucket and sponge. She sees a fireman sitting in the front seat. He smiles at her and says hello. He is very kind. He asks her what she is doing. Lily says she wants to wash his vehicle.

The fireman laughs and says that is very nice of her, but he has to go soon. He has to help people who are in trouble. He says she can wash one part of his vehicle, but not the whole thing. He shows her the wheel. He says she can wash the wheel, but she has to be careful and not get wet.

Lily agrees and starts to wash the wheel. She rubs the sponge on the tire and the hubcap. She makes them sparkle and squeak. She is very happy and proud. The fireman thanks her and gives her a sticker. He says she is a good helper and a good friend. He says goodbye and drives away.

Lily waves at him and watches him go. She hears the siren and sees the lights. She thinks he is very brave and nice. She goes back to her toy vehicles and washes them again. She pretends they are fire engines too. She has a lot of fun.

Lily likes to play with her dolls. She has many dolls, but her favorite is Anna. Anna has long hair and a pink dress. Lily likes to tie Anna's hair with a rubber. She makes a ponytail or a braid or a bun. She thinks Anna looks perfect.

One day, Lily wants to play with Anna outside. She puts on her shoes and coat and takes Anna with her. She sees a big tree in the yard. She thinks it would be fun to climb the tree with Anna. She holds Anna in one hand and climbs with the other.

She reaches a high branch and sits on it. She looks around and feels happy. She puts Anna next to her and ties her hair with a rubber again. She says, "You are perfect, Anna. I love you." She hugs Anna and smiles.

But then, she hears a loud noise. It is a dog. The dog sees Lily and Anna on the tree. The dog likes to chase things. The dog barks and jumps and tries to reach the tree. Lily feels scared. She holds Anna tight and says, "Go away, dog! Leave us alone!"

The dog does not listen. The dog keeps barking and jumping. Lily does not know what to do. She wants to go down, but the dog is too close. She wants to call for help, but no one is around. She feels sad and cries.

Then, she sees her mom. Her mom hears Lily and Anna and the dog. Her mom runs to the yard and sees what is happening. Her mom says, "Lily, don't worry. I'm here. I'll help you." Her mom picks up a stick and waves it at the dog. She says, "Shoo, dog! Go away! This is not your tree!" The dog sees the stick and feels scared. The dog stops barking and jumping. The dog runs away.

Lily sees her mom and feels happy. She says, "Mom, thank you! You saved us!" Her mom says, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you're okay." Her mom climbs the tree and reaches Lily and Anna. She says, "Come on, let's go down. It's not safe to play on the tree." She takes Lily and Anna in her arms and climbs down.

Lily hugs her mom and says, "I love you, mom. You are perfect." Her mom hugs her back and says, "I love you too, Lily. You are perfect." They go inside and have a snack. Lily plays with Anna and ties her hair with a rubber again. She says, "You are perfect, Anna. You are my best friend." Anna smiles and says, "You are perfect, Lily. You are my best friend too." They are happy. The end.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a big bucket of water and some cups. They liked to fill the cups and pour the water on the flowers, the grass and each other.

"Look, Lily, I can soak you!" Ben said, as he splashed some water on his sister.

"No, I can soak you more!" Lily said, and threw a cup of water at Ben.

They laughed and ran around, getting wet and having fun.

But then they saw their dad coming. He was bald and had a big beard. He looked angry.

"What are you doing, kids? You are making a mess!" he said.

"Sorry, dad, we were just playing," Ben said.

"Yeah, we like water," Lily said.

"Well, water is good, but not when you waste it and make the garden muddy. And look at you, you are soaked! You need to dry off and change your clothes. And be quiet, your mom is sleeping," dad said.

He took them inside and gave them towels and clean clothes. He was not so angry anymore, but he still wanted them to be quiet.

Ben and Lily dried off and changed. They felt a little cold and sorry. They decided to play something else, something quiet, like puzzles or books.

They loved their dad, even when he was bald and angry. They knew he loved them too, even when he was wet and muddy.

Anna and Ben are playing with a ball in the park. They like to pass the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they throw the ball high in the air and watch it fall. Sometimes they roll the ball on the grass and chase it.

"Pass me the ball, Ben!" Anna says. She holds out her hands and waits for the ball.

"OK, Anna!" Ben says. He picks up the ball and throws it to Anna. But he throws it too hard and too far. The ball flies over Anna's head and lands in a tree.

"Oh no, Ben! The ball is stuck in the tree!" Anna says. She runs to the tree and looks up. She sees the ball between some green leaves. She also sees something else. It is round and green and has a funny smell. It is a lime.

"Look, Ben! There is a lime in the tree too!" Anna says. She points to the lime.

"What is a lime?" Ben asks. He runs to the tree and looks up. He sees the lime next to the ball.

"A lime is a fruit. It is sour and juicy. You can squeeze it and make a drink. Or you can eat it if you like." Anna says. She has seen limes before at the market with her mom.

"Can we get the ball and the lime?" Ben asks. He wants to try the lime.

"Maybe. But it is not easy. The tree is tall and the branches are thin. We need something to help us." Anna says. She looks around and sees a long stick on the ground.

"Let's use the stick!" Ben says. He picks up the stick and gives it to Anna.

"OK, let me try." Anna says. She takes the stick and reaches up to the tree. She pokes the ball and the lime with the stick. The ball and the lime move a little, but they do not fall.

"Try harder, Anna!" Ben says. He cheers for Anna.

Anna tries harder. She pokes the ball and the lime again and again. Finally, the ball and the lime fall from the tree. They land on the grass.

"Yay, we did it!" Anna and Ben say. They run to the ball and the lime. They pick them up and hug them.

"Let's play with the ball again!" Ben says. He throws the ball to Anna.

"OK, but first let's try the lime!" Anna says. She peels the lime and breaks it in half. She gives one half to Ben and keeps one half for herself.

They bite the lime and make a funny face. The lime is sour and makes their mouth pucker.

"Ew, the lime is too sour!" Ben says. He spits out the lime.

"I like the lime. It is yummy!" Anna says. She eats the lime.

They laugh and play with the ball and the lime. They have fun in the park.

Sara and Ben like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They race them on the floor and make noises like vroom and beep.

One day, Sara finds a shiny screw on the floor. She thinks it is very fancy and pretty. She picks it up and puts it in her pocket.

"Look, Ben, I found a screw!" she says. "It is so fancy. I will keep it for myself."

Ben looks at the screw and wants it too. He thinks it is cool and can make his cars go faster. He tries to take it from Sara.

"No, Ben, it is mine!" Sara says. "I found it first. You have to find your own screw."

They start to fight over the screw. They pull and tug and shout. They are not happy.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the screw and takes it from them.

"Stop, Sara and Ben!" she says. "This is not a toy. This is a screw. It can hurt you if you play with it. It belongs to Dad. He needs it to fix the lamp."

She gives the screw to Dad and tells Sara and Ben to share their toys. She gives them each a hug and a cookie.

Sara and Ben say sorry to each other and to Mom and Dad. They decide to play with their cars again. They forget about the screw and have fun. They are happy.

Sam does not care. He laughs and runs away with some blocks. He thinks he is clever and strong. He does not have any friends.

One day, it was very cold. The log had snow on it. Lila and Tom put on their hats and gloves and ran to the park. They wanted to balance on the log again.

But the log was slippery. Lila went first. She tried to walk on the log, but she slipped and fell. She landed in the snow. She was wet and filthy.

"I'm okay, but I'm cold and dirty," Lila said. She shivered and brushed off the snow.

"Let's go home and get warm and clean," Tom said. He helped her up. They held hands and walked back to their house.

"Look, I have a hat!" Lily said, putting a sock on her head.

They threw more laundry at each other, making a big mess. They did not hear their mom calling them for lunch.

"Uh-oh, we made a mess," Ben said.

"Mom will be mad," Lily said.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the farm with their mom and dad. They wanted to see the animals and play in the grass. They saw chickens, pigs, horses and sheep. They liked to watch them and hear their sounds.

"Look, there is a cow!" Lily said, pointing to a big black and white animal. "Can we go and say hello?"

"Sure, but be careful and gentle," mom said. "Cows are very big and sometimes shy."

Tom and Lily walked slowly to the cow. She was eating some hay and did not notice them at first. They reached out their hands and touched her soft fur. She looked at them with her big brown eyes and mooed.

"Hello, cow," Tom said. "You are amazing. You are so big and soft and you make milk. Can we be your friends?"

The cow nodded and licked Tom's face with her tongue. He giggled and hugged her neck. Lily did the same. They felt happy and warm.

"Wow, you are so brave and kind," dad said, taking a picture of them. "You made a new friend today. What do you want to name her?"

Tom and Lily thought for a moment. Then they said together, "We want to name her Daisy. She is our amazing cow."

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Anna had a doll and Ben had a car. They were having fun until Ben saw Anna's doll and wanted to play with it.

"Give me your doll!" Ben said, grabbing the doll from Anna's hands.

"No, it's mine!" Anna said, pulling the doll back.

They both tugged and pulled on the doll until it ripped in half. Anna and Ben looked at the broken doll and started to cry.

"Look what you did!" Anna said, pointing her finger at Ben.

"It's your fault!" Ben said, pointing his finger at Anna.

They were both very stubborn and did not want to say sorry. They turned away from each other and sat on opposite sides of the room, still crying.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken doll and the two angry children.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

"Ben broke my doll!" Anna said.

"Anna broke my car!" Ben said.

Mom shook her head and sighed. She picked up the pieces of the doll and the car and put them on the table.

"I'm sorry your toys are broken, but you can't blame each other. You both need to share and be nice to each other. Can you say sorry and hug?" Mom said.

Anna and Ben looked at each other and felt a little sorry. They knew Mom was right. They slowly got up and walked towards each other.

"I'm sorry, Anna," Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Anna said.

They hugged and smiled. Mom smiled too.

"That's better. Now, let's see if we can fix your toys. Maybe we can return them to how they were before," Mom said.

She took some glue and tape and started to mend the doll and the car. Anna and Ben helped her and watched as their toys came back together.

"Thank you, Mom," Anna and Ben said.

"You're welcome, my loves. Now, how about we play together with your toys?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom," Anna and Ben said.

They took their toys and played happily in the living room. They learned to share and be nice to each other. They were not stubborn anymore.
